A few hours later, the helicopter flew us back to Griffin.
Grizzly gave a quick rundown of the situation, and our last mission as Squad Grizzly was over. After the Commander left, even if we stayed at Griffin, things had changed...
Grizzly suggested we all get together one last time before disbanding to mark the end of our time at Griffin and get ready for a new beginning.
There was no reason to say no, so I agreed.

The meetup spot was in a small grove a short distance away from Griffin headquarters.
On the agreed day, I brought the projector and speakers as Grizzly had asked and arrived right on time. PzB39 was carrying a bunch of action movie DVDs, carefully guarding them like a penguin guarding an egg. M590 was helping with PzB39's motorbike, which had new graffiti on it—a cute plush brown bear. It was obvious who had done it. Grizz brought a few bottles of beer, and I knew they were for me. M82 had prepared a whole box of fireworks. The box was so tall it completely hid her face, but I could still tell she was in a good mood from her cheerful steps.
All of Griffin was wrapped in the sadness of farewells, but my teammates didn't seem to feel that way. Maybe it was because we had all planned to go to the Green Zone together. What they didn't know was that I hadn't submitted my application yet. I was still hesitating.

I put the projector down and set it up absentmindedly. The beam of the projector hit a dense patch of leaves, like a natural screen. PzB39 put the disc in place. After a small hiss, a certain over the top theme song blasted from the speakers.
M82 opened a bottle of beer for me. This time, my olfactory module picked up the fresh smell of malt and hops. I closed my eyes and drank the whole bottle of beer.
Watching everyone bustling around, I tried to voice my concerns.
"So... why are we all going to the Green Zone? There's nothing wrong with staying in Griffin, right?"
"There's nothing wrong with that, but there are too few spots to stay in Griffin, and we can do more in the Green Zone!"
"Yeah, my motorbike needs more modifications. High-horsepower acceleration is essential for it. If I stay in Griffin, how will I have time to modify it?"
"Griffin's database doesn't have as many sci-fi novels as the city library..."
My teammates answered my questions rather flippantly.

"But the Green Zone isn't always safe. Just like last time, we almost got hurt during the mission. That Doll named Claire also—"
"Events like that are so rare, they barely happen once a year!"
"Yeah, Alfa, what's up with you today? You're overthinking things. This isn't like you."
"Exactly! Normally, you'd already be dragging PzB to find a good spot to watch the stars. You did say you wanted to see that thing this year, something Mercury...? What was it again...?"
"The transit of Mercury."
I couldn't help but add.
"Yes! That. You're really acting strange today, Alfa. Are you hiding something from us?"
Looking at my teammates' faces of genuine concern, I opened my mouth, but I found myself unable to voice my misgivings.
I need more time to figure this out.
What I know for sure is that my teammates are all excited about their future in the Green Zone, but...
Claire's empty eyes still linger in my mind.
How can I convince them to stay, and is it really right to ask them to? Staying at Griffin means continuing to fight, and those beautiful dreams about the future will vanish.
This isn't the outcome I desire.

"Alfa, what's up with you? You keep making different faces. It's as if you've used up a year's worth of expressions tonight."
"Oh, I'm fine. I got really excited when you mentioned the transit of Mercury. Yeah, that's it."
"Just because of that? Well, it's hard to understand, but I'm really into modifying motorbikes myself, so I can't really judge you... Once we get to the Green Zone, we'll have plenty of time to mess around with our own hobbies."
...
My teammates' kind attempts to smooth things over made me feel even guiltier, and before I knew it, I'd downed another bottle of beer.
If I stay behind and use Griffin's power to help everyone when needed, and let Grizzly and the others go to the Green Zone, would that be the best solution?
My hand holding the beer bottle twitched when this idea emerged. It's definitely doable. As long as the reorganized Griffin can ensure the supply of provisions, provide the necessary frame maintenance, and also give me some free time, this plan can solve all problems in one go.
But another issue immediately came to mind—
If I stay at Griffin alone, it means I'll be breaking my previous promise. I had promised to go to the Green Zone with the rest of the team...

Right now, I really wish that person were still at Griffin, so I could knock on their door for answers.
But that's not possible... and if the Commander were still in Griffin, the choice we would have made was obvious.

Just as I was feeling conflicted, M82 lit the fireworks. A golden lion with bared fangs and claws roared fiercely in the sky, a motorbike leapt across a gap and soared through the air, and the bright arm of a galaxy sprang out of a thick open book. Fireworks ignited one by one, and finally Squad Grizzly's logo was fixed in the night sky before it slowly faded and went out softly in the night breeze.
The team logo was pretty simple. We drew it together when the team was formed. Everyone added a stroke, and the final product looked kind of odd. The so-called majestic brown bear actually looked more like a chubby big cat.
At first, my teammates cheered, then they gradually fell silent. In the end, we all held hands and watched the custom fireworks show together.
"A fine commemoration, is it not?"
M82 asked softly.
I quickly nodded.

Perhaps it was because we missed the days at Griffin, or perhaps it was the mesmerizing patterns. After the fireworks ended, no one left right away. We kept changing out the discs on the projector, chatting about the past and the future.
I sat on a hill not too far from them—they were already used to me keeping my distance.
The soft cloth beneath me was dry and clean. I lay down gently and gazed up at the night sky. The stars were vast and countless as they shone brightly. The cool night breeze gradually blew away the noise from my teammates.
Even though it was the perfect place to think in peace and quiet, I found myself unable to calm down.

Stay at Griffin or accept reassignment?
Staying at Griffin means I can keep protecting everyone.
Accepting reassignment means I can keep my original promise. Like Grizzly said in the beginning, as long as we're all together, Squad Grizzly hasn't really disbanded.

My neural cloud has already arrived at the most reasonable conclusion, but I just can't seem to take that step, and I can't honestly share my worries with Grizzly and the others. If they knew I chose to stay, they'd definitely stick with me, but I can't be the one to crush those dreams.
...
Looking at the vast starry sky, I gently asked the stars, "Can you tell me what I should do...?"
With the Commander not here, I have only them to ask.
My question went unanswered. Only the night wind blew gently, lifting my long hair.
"I guess I have a lot of time tonight to think about this..."
I turned over and hugged my knees to my chest.

\"Commander, would you like to taste my:
"Commander, would you like to taste my cooking?"

This was the first time Groza was cooking for the Commander, and clearly even she was surprised by that. Even if the Commander was used to having an extra Doll aboard the Elmo, but even so—

"Oh? Does my attire look so strange?" 

The apron-clad Groza flashed a smile that said she was expecting this reaction and placed the pumpkin pie she made on the table.

"...I was just wondering when we got a housekeeper Doll on the Elmo."

The Commander pulled up a chair and sat down, and Groza took a seat beside her.

"Since it's my first time cooking for you, I thought I should dress for the occasion. How is it? Does it suit me?" Groza smiled at the Commander.
"It does, very much so."

The Commander shifted her gaze from Groza to the pumpkin pie sitting on the plate. The crust had been baked to a rich brown color, and it looked crispy and delicious. Meanwhile, the filling looked soft and moist, gleaming in the light and radiating a tempting aroma.

"Commander? You should taste it rather than just staring at it," said Groza while gesturing for the Commander to help herself.

The Commander didn't hesitate, taking a slice of the pie and putting it in her mouth. 
—It tasted nothing like they imagined. A complex taste akin to vomit spread through their mouth. The crispy crust and the filling blended together, leading to even more ghastly mental images.

"..."
"Commander?"

The Commander forced it down, then thought carefully before speaking.

"Have you tried it yourself, Groza?"
"Not at the moment. In truth, I was planning to request that you install gastral modules in me." Despite her doubts, Groza voiced her thoughts without holding back.
"Got it, I'll install them in tomorrow."

27 September 2069, 1905hrs\nWhy is she s:
27 September 2069, 1905hrs
Why is she so unbearably slow? What is SV-98 doing? It's been 35 minutes past our agreed time. Isn't she always meticulous and punctual? Why is she standing me up this time?
Hmph, when she arrives, I’ll need to ask her what could be more important than our "special mission."

After leaving Griffin, SV-98 and I were unsure of where to go. We happened to come across an Intercontinental Railway train that was recruiting security personnel. They mentioned being supplied with unlimited power and the chance to take short trips outside upon arrival at train stations. Such opportunities are rare.
We applied and got accepted—what’s the train called? KW16? KW16? Hmm, from Kryvyi Rih to Vilnius, it takes 30 hours. We'll arrive tomorrow.
 
The work of the security team is quite monotonous—just security checks and patrols, with each shift lasting for dozens of hours.
To keep ourselves from getting rusty, SV-98 and I agreed on a "special mission."
Every day at 1830hrs, we meet on top of train carriage 23. Our goal is to enjoy the scenery together.

How about that? It’s a brilliant idea, isn’t it? SV-98 looked forward to it every day.

...I hear the sound of someone climbing the ladder from below. It must be SV-98.
"Sorry, SVD, I'm late."
"SV-98! Do you have any idea how long I waited for you?"
"Sorry, sorry. I kept you waiting for 38 minutes and 42 seconds. I should have arrived on time, but the charging stations were occupied by passengers, so I had to wait in line for 36 minutes..."
"Oh, well, if it was for charging, then there's nothing you could have done... Wait a minute, why did you obediently wait for the passengers to finish charging? The charging stations in the dining car are for Dolls only! Just kick the passengers out and use it yourself!"
"Kick... kick the passengers out?
That doesn't seem right. The train manual states that we should respect the passengers and prioritize their rights..."
"Alright, alright, next time that happens, come straight to me!"
"Okay, I'm glad you understand. Actually, while waiting, I spotted an old book called [Watchman] on the nearby magazine rack. It was quite interesting."
"[Watchman]? What's it about?"
"It tells the story of a person who guards their homeland, refusing to leave despite terrible storms and wars. I only read a small part of it, but I really liked the name 'Watchman'."
"Hmm, it does sound cool. You know, we watch over this plain every day. Doesn’t that make us the Watchmen of it? Oh, and... Didn’t we talk about choosing new names earlier? "'Watchman' sounds good, So I'll take that name~"
"SVD, are you serious?"
"You're doubting me? Of course I'm serious! Ahem—yes. The name 'Watchman' belongs to me from now on."
"...Lady... Watchman...?"
 
Tsk, what did SV-98 mean by that? She even added 'Lady' on purpose. 
 
"I’m serious—call me Watchman!"
"...Alright, Lady Watchman."
"Hey—! It's Watchman!"

Despite several corrections, SV-98 insisted on calling me Lady Watchman. Hmph, I bet she wants the name for herself and is teasing me on purpose.
With the special mission over, I'm feeling much better. Today’s special mission was complete, so it was time to head back to the carriage.

...!
 
Was that... an explosion?!
The train brakes suddenly, and I almost lose my balance. Why did the train stop all of a sudden? If it was a temporary stop, there should have been an announcement by now—but there's nothing at all?
The passengers around me are in a state of panic. I quickly try to calm them down, telling them to stay seated and not to panic, but I can’t find SV-98 anywhere. Where is she? She might not have reacted as quickly as I did and could be hurt. I need to contact her quickly—static? Unable to connect?
Just as I was about to try calling her again, the Captain's voice came in through the communicator—this is bad, it's the Varjagers!
27 September, 2069, 2115hrs\nWe are bein:
27 September, 2069, 2115hrs
We are being attacked by the Varjagers.
 
Captain issued the order to engage over the comms. After relinquishing the care of the frightened young passengers to the train staff, I quickly climb onto the roof of the nearest railcar.
The front of the train is shrouded in smoke, making it impossible to determine the extent of the damage.
I heard about the Varjager attacking the intercontinental railway before, but experiencing it firsthand? This is a first.
I nervously look around; where did SVD go?
I hope she's fine. Experienced as she is, she likely doesn't require my worries.
 
Their convoy arrives. In a few short seconds, the Varjagers' convoy will enter my firing range.
3, 2... they've stopped? The leading armored vehicle comes to a halt, no longer advancing. The jeeps behind it also turn around and head towards the rear of the train. What are they looking for in the back?
Intercontinental trains are typically divided into two sections: the front half for passengers and the rear half for cargo.
This train's cargo section carries enough supplies to sustain the residents of Vilnius for half a month.
In addition, I notice a number of distinctive cargo containers usually holding military supplies. It seems these are their targets.
 
Time is running out. Just as I'm moving out to the rear of the train, the armored vehicle suddenly accelerates and heads toward the front of the train. A large-caliber howitzer, even 
bigger than their previous rocket launcher, is being mounted and aimed directly at the tracks.
Could it be that they aim to not only steal the supplies but also destroy the tracks? I need to report this to the Captain immediately.
Where's my terminal? It was right here moments ago.
 
The smoke in front is slowly clearing. I inspect the tracks, and although the emergency brake was triggered in fear of derailing, the tracks themselves are not severely damaged. With some quick repairs after driving off the Varjagers, we should be able to proceed without a problem. Another hit, however, will leave us stranded. 
An intercontinental railway train can not stop in the Yellow Zone. 
After a brief moment of contemplation, I determine that the priority is to prevent the tracks from being damaged again. Everyone else has gone after the jeeps heading to the rear; I'm the only one remaining here in the front.
With my firepower, the only way to stop them is to either take out the crew of the armored vehicle or destroy the howitzer itself. Alright, range, check. Angle, check... All I need now is to move another five meters forward...
Not good, the howitzer is already loaded. Should I keep my head down? If I give up now, the tracks will be blown up!
No, I won't back down; instead, I stay put in place and keep my aim steady. If only sacrificing my body is enough to stop them...

...！
My vision blurs and my shot went off target—damn it.
An explosion rings out from the front of the train, the tremendous force throws me to the ground before making me tumble a few times.
"What are you doing, daydreaming? Don't you know to get out of the way when a shell is coming at your face?!"
"...SVD... what are you doing here?"
"What am I doing? Hmph, without me, you'd have been blown to bits! Also, remember to call me Watchman."
"...Lady Watchman, according to my calculations, I had a 70% chance of intercepting the incoming shell. While it would have damaged my body, that is acceptable compared to the tracks being destroyed. Hadn't you interrupted..."
"Stop, stop! Your calculations are nuts! And you're blaming me for getting in your way? Also, it's Watchman!"
"...Sorry."
SVD—no, according to her request, she's now "Watchman", but this is still quite a mouthful name, which is why I added "Lady" in front, hoping she'd realize my discontent.
SVD's computing powers aren't exceptional, so it's understandable that she can't grasp my plan. Besides, she did save me.
After snatching our supplies, the Varjagers quickly retreats. In the end, we only manage to damage two jeeps and recover three boxes of supplies.
The Intercontinental train's exterior is made of special materials impervious to explosives, so luckily the passengers only suffered minor injuries from the emergency brake.
The bad news is, the tracks are completely destroyed, and the train can't journey on. Had I been able to intercept that last shell... I shake my head. What's done is done. I need to accept it and deal with the consequences. The security team's Dolls are severely damaged during the defense, leaving only Lady Watchman and me relatively unscathed.
The Captain tasks me with going the nearest stopover station to seek assistance, and Lady Watchman requests to join me.
..."Lady Watchman" worries too much sometimes.

With the most experience and an undefeated record under their belt, Cassius was elected as the team leader with no objections. After discussing with the others—mainly just Cassius and I—we developed the plan for this operation. 

As a precautionary measure, we didn't put all our faith in the unreliable IFF device. Instead, we brought some heavy firepower and enough supplies to last a month per our standard procedure. 
Since we needed to recover materials in addition to firepower and supplies, we also prepared two empty jeeps. Adding to them the vehicles to transport the combat personnel, a total of five vehicles, just enough to be considered a convoy. 
With the slower pace of large-scale movements in mind, Musk and I, both well-versed in covert operations, would arrive at the target location first as vanguards while the others followed with weapons and supplies. 

After driving at full speed for an entire day and night, we found ourselves only a few kilometers away from the target location. Although the landscape was still dominated by yellow sand, there were at least some withered trees and hills in sight. 
"Musk, stop here and get out." 
"What? We're still quite far away. Look at the map—we’re two or three klicks from the designated coordinates. Why are we stopping here?" 
"We're here to scout. We don't know that Doll's operating range yet. If we drive in and run into it head-on, then would you know whether we should engage with it or not?" 
"I don't suppose we have a choice if we do run into it. Fine, you're the strategist, it's your call!" 
We set the vehicle up as a base two kilometers off the target location then proceeded on foot towards QE934DW-H17TR7. 

A single naturally formed cave in the hillside could be found at the site. We found ourselves a location with an elevation difference, a clear view, and good concealment. 
"Hey, hey! Do you see at all that clutter piled up in front of the cave?" 
"I can't see it clearly. Let me adjust my binoculars." 
"It's all kinds of fucked up. Looks like severed limbs... Eww! ELID remains too! ...Gosh, with both human and ELID corpses strewn about, just what kind of monster lives there?" 
"Don't give yourself a scare. Let's just wait and see." 
Two hours went by with no signs of activity. 
"Is that Doll really here? Not a thing showed up even after waiting for so long." 
"Musk, you've had experience in doing this kind of thing before, just hang in there. We've barely even started." 

Several hours later, the sky gradually darkened as dusk set in.
"Brr... It's getting chilly. Hey, what was that?!" 
"Quiet... What's the big deal?" 
"Did you see that, Shuld?" 
"See what? Has your brain frozen over or what?" 
"No way in hell... Looked like something atop that corpse pile was moving..." 
"Don't scare me... I'm an atheist, just so you know." 
I held my breath, carefully watching the pile of corpses. It seemed like something on top was really moving! 
"Wait, something's coming out! It's got two sharp protrusions on its head..." 
"Feels like it's moving things... Damn! It's stacking those corpses up! Ah! It disappeared!" 
It darted away with such speed that it appeared to vanish from our view in an instant. 
"With those kinds of ears, could it be a fox? Tch... being in a contamination zone, it must've mutated long ago!" 
"If it really was a fox, it'd be a Boojum by now with that kind of agility. Do you think we'd still be chatting like this if that's the case? It would've ripped us apart by now!" 
"Makes sense. I think it might be the Doll we're looking for. Should we chase after it, Mr. Strategist?" 
"No, remember, our mission is only to keep an eye out." 

A few minutes later, it returned. 
This time, it lingered for longer, allowing us to discern that it was a female Doll wrapped in a cloak. 
"See, I told you it was a Doll!" 
The Doll cautiously looked around at the cave entrance for a moment, then promptly entered the cave, never to be seen coming out again. 
"What's with this Doll? Appearing and disappearing like that, it’s going to scare me into an early grave. She must be our target, right?" 
"Not sure. We need Cassius and the IFF device to confirm. It's getting really cold. Let's head back." 
"What? So, we're not keeping a watch during the night?" 
"We've done enough for today." 
Back at our base, I reviewed the intel collected today: A small, extremely fast Doll with ear-like protrusions on its head; displays peculiar behavior; appears harmless for now, but vigilance is required. 
After sending the information to Cassius who was still on the way, I packed up my things for the night and quickly went to sleep.

Mechty has a text file in her personal terminal called "The Book of Grudges", containing random musings and snarky comments about all sorts of things.

"That Klukai! She's a devil! She gave me an extra hour of training! A WHOLE EXTRA HOUR! Both my soul and my body are in ruins now..."

"According to Dier's records, Klukai has been using the switch in a perfectly sensible way. Her toggling of your high output mode has been beneficial to your frame operations. After all, even the best computer will rot away if you keep it switched off."
"How, how could this be..."
Mechty collapsed onto her bean bag sofa in despair.
"Mechty, have you ever thought about what would happen if Klukai went out for a mission and didn't come back? You're the next most senior member in the squad; what would you do then? Perhaps all the demands Klukai has made of you were intended to address that situation, hm?"
Die? That Klukai? How could that even happen...
"What should I do? What can I even do? If something happened that managed to take even her out, I'd probably be taking a dirt nap myself..."
Little did Mechty know that she would face such a situation in the near future.
\"(Sob) Wake up, Big Sis Klukai—what sho:
"(Sob) Wake up, Big Sis Klukai—what should we do? Is 404 doomed to be wiped out here? Dammit, I'm going to give those baldies the fight of their lives!"
"B-B-B-B-B-Belka! Calm down, I think... I think it'd be better not to shake Leader Klukai so ha-ha-ha-ha—"
Fear, anger, and confusion fill this place—A certain tiny room that a group of illegal Dolls are using as a workshop.
Before Mechty's eyes is Klukai, whose frame systems have been severely damaged. There is also Belka, who is beside herself in panic, and Andoris, who has just crashed while trying to process the situation.
Outside the room are several hundred Doll frames that are about to self-destruct.
Meanwhile, Leva's words echo inside Mechty's neural cloud—
"You're the next most senior member in the squad; what would you do then?"
Wait, was that day today?
Am I the only member of the original Squad 404 that's left?
...If I just lie back at a time like this... We'll truly be done for.
At this point, Mechty quickly moves into action.
"Belka, get a hold of yourself! Klukai's only gone into forced shutdown mode for the time being! Once we get out of here, fixing her will be a piece of cake!"
"R-Really? So Big Sis Klukai won't forget the records of us fighting side by side?"
"Heck no! I've lost so many frames over the years that I can confidently say damage like this doesn't warrant a frame swap."
"You, you've lost many frames over the years...?"
Right, that's Belka sorted! Next up...
Mechty hugs Andoris around her waist. Judging by how her pupils are contracting and dilating, she should come back online in three, two, one—
"—rd? Huh? Did I just crash again? I hope it wasn't for too long this time..."

"Will do, I'm sending the distress signal now."
After ensuring that her teammates have their heads back in the game, Mechty can't help but begin thinking about their escape route.
Much as she hates to admit it, she has to agree that Klukai dragging her along to after-action reviews turned out to be useful after all. Even the most annoying and boring nagging will stick in the mind if it's repeated a hundred times; even the most difficult path ends up becoming easy when you've walked it a thousand times before.
Right now, it's as though Mechty is operating entirely on routine; she's even acting in a somewhat brisk and professional way.
There's a mix of emotions in Mechty's neural cloud as she looks at Klukai, who's resting on Belka's back.
"Alright, I admit it. Klukai did the right thing, just this once..."
She feels around Klukai's body for the switch.
"Now then, this veteran of the old 404 will help clear a path... for the rest of you... Ehh..."
—After the successful conclusion of that mission, Leva kept needling Mechty about that line which could have come straight from a shonen manga.
After a hard day's work, I accepted Mech:
After a hard day's work, I accepted Mechty's invitation to watch a movie with her.
We'd be watching a horror movie.
In order to help add to the atmosphere, we turned off the lights and drew the curtains shut so the room was filled with darkness, lit only by the ghostly blue light of the projector screen.
However—
"...Hey, isn't this stage blood TOO bright? Doesn't look like blood at all."
"Ah... yeah, I think so too, Commander. Also, the way they're trying to farm scares is way too clichéd... Like, you'd think they'd have learned not to pull off such obvious jumpscares after so many years, right..."
Maybe it's because I've been watching too many horror movies with Mechty, but I've begun to nitpick them right beside her.
"...Man, this isn't scary at all... Are you disappointed, Commander?"
"Hm? I think it's okay. It's good for relaxing, if nothing else."
"Hmm... In that case... let's spice things up a little."
"Wait, what do you—"
Before I can finish, I feel something burrow into my arms.
When I look down, I see Mechty's fluffy head pressed against my chest, lit by the reflections from the silver screen.
"Uwah! Commander, save me, I'm so scared... gyaaah... I..."
"...You're not selling this at all. Also—"
I pat Mechty's head, but the moment she looks up, I momentarily forget to breathe; there's a pale, ghoulish face with dark red tearstreaks from its eyes right in front of me."
"Uwaaahhh—Now THAT's a proper jumpscare!"
"..."
"Hahaha, how was that? Took me a long time to get this monster makeup just right, and even longer to figure out how to quickly apply it in the dark. Looks like it'll do well as a sideshow for Halloween this year..."
"...Commander?"
"(Coughs) Uh, it's a good idea, but you shouldn't do that in front of Klukai."
"Oh... Yeah, you're right, if I scare her, she'll get mad about being embarrassed in public. When that happens... I might end up becoming a real ghost myself... Wait, can Dolls become ghosts..."
After seeing that Mechty has been successfully distracted, I surreptitiously force my pounding heart to calm down.
Nope, wasn't scared, not at all.
After I sang my praises of Mechty's armc:

"Why did you buy so many at once?"
"Well, I have different beanbags for different occasions. Take this one for example—"
Mechty sat down on one that was shaped like a cloud.
"I use this one when gaming because it has two fluffy pads on the sides that work as armrests."
"Hm, you have a point. That way you won't get tired while holding your joypad."
"Hehe, I know, right? And then... There's this coffin-shaped one. You can zip it up from the inside and it has great noise cancellation properties~"
"Maybe not that one..."
"Ohhhh, come try this one, Commander. I think this is the most interesting of the lot."
Mechty drags me over to a beanbag that looks like a huge sausage roll. After pushing me in there, she works her way inside until she's shoulder-to-shoulder with me.
"So... what's so special about this one?"
"Hang on, Commander..."
Mechty rummages around inside the bread beanbag and pulls out a pickle-shaped pillow and a blanket with a cheese-dip pattern on it that she pulls over the two of us.
"Change— hotdog!"

I pause for a moment, and then I can't help giggling.
"Ah, Commander, you're laughing... Alright then, though it pains me, I shall give this hotdog beanbag to you!"
"Hahaha, thank you, but there are two sausages inside this hotdog. Don't you think that's being a little too generous?"

\"You really like gaming, don't you, Mec:

It is a gently-sunlit afternoon, and I can't help but sigh as I watch Mechty gaming in the lounge.
"Well... games are fun. You can experience all sorts of things through them, and..."
Mechty turns over in her bean bag sofa and puts down her controller. Her usually drooping eyes are serious now.
"...And I managed to meet you because of games like this, Commander."
"..."
"At first, I was nothing more than a pile of cold data and programming code."
"In order to meet you, my artist designed a concept for me, my writer fleshed me out, and my voice actor imbued me with emotion..."

"..."

"Oh hey, looks like you cleared 'The Real Adventures of the Electronic Ghost.'"

"Well, you did a good job. For a moment I felt like the game was real."

Appendix 2: Tactical Deployment by Warra: Appendix 2: Tactical Deployment by Warrant Officer Vladimir
When the Nemertea attacked the Great Wal:
When the Nemertea attacked the Great Wall Railway, Warrant Officer Vladimir carried out his duties by issuing a series of orders aimed at repelling the attack.
However, Vladimir's deployments yielded minimal impact for the subsequent reasons:
1. HQ's failure to obtain real-time information on the situation at the frontline.
2. Defense garrison's total lack of preparation for the Nemertea's attack.
3. Warrant Officer Vladimir's unfamiliarity with the Nemertea's attack patterns.
These factors contributed to Warrant Officer Vladimir's failure to make timely and appropriate decisions.
At the time, a severe Collapse storm was occurring in the W_2069_0105 region, resulting in extremely low outdoor visibility and interference with communication equipment. Communication within the train was also disrupted, preventing HQ, located far from Nemertea's attack site, from accessing the threat promptly.
The following footage from the train's CCTV system supports this point.

#Start of Recording
The footage from this car is blurry, making distinguishing humans from Dolls challenging. The sound of gunfire is very clear.
00:00:27 "North! Deploy Paladin multi-role Dolls to the north! That thing came from the north!"
00:00:54 "Open the door! COME ON, open the door, we're from car CZ-3!" 
After the door opens, the footage shows a soldier helping a wounded comrade into the car.
00:01:07 "CZ-3 is finished. That Boojum overturned the car. We're the only ones who survived!
Our shit can't kill it. We need to retreat!"
00:01:30 "Forget retreating. If we don't stop it here, that giant worm will overturn the entire train and it's we'll all DONE! Where's Kimilov? Find him! Have him take the wounded away then head to the command car to notify our Warrant Officer! Has communication been established yet?"
00:01:52 "No, all the channels are still nothing but damn static!"
00:02:18 "Then let..."
#End of Recording

At 2 minutes and 19 seconds, the footage showed a massive jolt followed by a blackout.
This car endured a massive impact, and the surveillance equipment was also damaged.
However, this footage has already demonstrated the suddenness of the Nemertea attack, the ineffectiveness of the defense garrison's counterattack, and Warrant Officer Vladimir's failure to get a hold of the situation in a timely manner due to various reasons. As a result, Warrant Officer Vladimir issued orders in haste without taking into account the specific circumstances at the frontline. 
After receiving the intelligence, Warrant Officer Vladimir ordered Sergeant Romonlosov to act as a courier and relay deployment orders to the forces in cars CZ-4 to CZ-9 and instructed maintenance personnel to expedite the repair of communication equipment to send reinforcement requests to multiple outposts.

Warrant Officer Vladimir's deployment orders were as follows:
1. Deploy 8 Paladin multirole Dolls as vanguards to delay the Nemertea's advance. Additionally, the Paladin multirole Dolls were to serve as the first line of defense for the Great Wall Railway train.
2. Deploy Fire Support Company with the crew instructed to position Coeus hover assault guns at various firing angles in order to maximize firepower for a saturated bombardment of the Nemertea's position.
3. Concentrate the Aegis series Dolls from the Combat Engineer Company into a defensive battalion and deploy them along the Nemertea's path of advance as the second line of defense behind the Paladin multirole Dolls.
4. Dispatch 2 Automated Forward Reconnaissance Companies to harass the Nemertea from the flanks, drawing its attention while using their mobility to evade its attacks. Aiming to delay Nemertea's advance and reduce losses to the assault Dolls battalion.
Warrant Officer Vladimir knew that the current equipment could not kill the Nemertea. Therefore, the tactical deployment aimed to delay the Nemertea as much as possible to buy time for reinforcements from the dispatch stations to arrive.

However, in practice, the Paladin multirole Dolls barely managed to slow the advance; too concentrated outside car CZ-4, allowing the Nemertea to destroy several of them while attacking that car. Subsequently, the Nemertea, with its broad attack range, eliminated all the reconnaissance Dolls and broke through the defense line of the Aegis series Dolls. The Cerynitis autonomous SPAA from the Automated Air Defense Company did not inflict significant damage on the Nemertea.

Given the situation, Warrant Officer Vladimir decided to personally operate a "Paladin" heavy defense Doll to draw the Nemertea away from the Great Wall Railway and prevent further damage. The following footage documents Warrant Officer Vladimir's final orders:

#Start of Recording
00:00:12 "Sir! That's suicide!"
00:00:33 "Everything has failed. Don't you get it? Someone must go out and lure the Nemertea away!"
00:00:39 "Going to where the Nemertea's attacking now is a certain death!"
00:00:43 "You have any other ideas? The reconnaissance companies are all gone. All we have left is me taking the 'Paladin' out to hold off the Nemertea."
00:00:47 "The others..."
00:00:55 "I'd rather wait for reinforcements from the dispatch stations."
00:01:03 "Whether the communication equipment will function in the Collapse storm is completely unknown!"
00:01:14 "Since internal communication has been restored, there is no reason to believe the support request was not sent."
00:01:27 "Sir, you have two months until your transfer. Why die here?"
00:01:35 "I'm still a soldier."
00:01:43 "Aren't you scared?"
00:01:52 "Of course I'm scared, just like you. But someone has to do it. Now transfer control of the 'Paladin' to me, Sergeant Burskin. That's an order."
#End of Recording

According to testimonies, Warrant Officer Vladimir indeed operated the 'Paladin' heavy defense Doll and charged into the Collapse storm, drawing Nemertea's attention.
Warrant Officer Vladimir's body was not found, but there is no reason to believe he survived.

From this incident, it can be concluded that the current railway garrison is severely underprepared for combat in Collapse storm environments and lacks backup communication equipment for such conditions. The tactical deployment also heavily relied on past experiences, which proved ineffective against large, high-threat Boojum such as the Nemertea.
Appendix 3: Attack Pattern Analysis of L: Appendix 3: Attack Pattern Analysis of Level V Boojum "Nemertea"
In this incident, the Nemertea demonstra:
In this incident, the Nemertea demonstrated considerable destructive power and resilience against the current weaponry of the Railway Defense Forces. The lack of understanding of Nemertea's attack patterns was a major factor contributing to the heavy casualties.
We obtained first-hand data on the Nemertea's attack from the train's external surveillance footage and analyzed its attack behavior patterns.

#Video start
00:02:24 The Nemertea advances rapidly while emitting eerie howls.
00:02:33 The middle section of the car is hit by the Nemertea, resulting in violent shaking.
00:02:56 The Nemertea strikes the carriage again and sprays an unidentified liquid from its maw.
#Video pause
This footage reveals the startling size of the Nemertea, with its towering body exceeding 20 meters in height, demonstrating surprising flexibility and physical strength. Although the Nemertea's mandibles are not strong enough to penetrate the 20mm steel plates of the Great Wall Railway, its formidable force is capable of shaking the large, sturdy carriages. This impact-based attack was the Nemertea's primary offense method during this incident.
#Video resume
00:05:11 The liquid sprayed by the Nemertea flows onto the stabilizer of the carriage.
00:05:38 The Nemertea strikes again, shaking the carriage until it is completely overturned.
00:05:47 Soldiers in the adjacent carriage open fire, but most of their bullets are deflected.
00:06:12 The Nemertea sprays liquid again.
#Video pause
This footage, along with the subsequent battlefield inspection report, reveals that the liquid sprayed by the Nemertea has a corrosive effect on metal. While it does not directly dissolve the outer walls of the carriages, it affects weaker components such as the stabilizers and related joints, compromising the stability of the carriages. Combined with the Nemertea's powerful impacts, this ultimately led to the collapse of the Great Wall Railway. Additionally, the Nemertea's thick skin made it highly resistant to conventional weaponry, which prevented its timely expulsion.
Additionally, the liquid sprayed by the Nemertea was found to be highly viscous.
Postmortem examinations revealed that some soldiers died from respiratory tract obstruction caused by this liquid.
#Video resume
00:30:32 The Nemertea continues to collide with adjacent carriages, delivering heavy damage to the Paladin multifunctional Dolls concentrated around the CZ-4 carriage. Dozens of ELIDs assault the gaps between the carriages.
#Video pause
The footage suggests that the Nemertea attracts nearby ELIDs, indicating a potential symbiotic relationship between them.

The analysis of the Nemertea's behavior reveals that it possesses high mobility, strong impact force, the ability to spray highly viscous corrosive liquid, thick skin, and a potential symbiotic relationship with the ELIDs it attracts.
In this incident, the Railway Defense Forces' failure to promptly understand Nemertea's characteristics ultimately resulted in irreparable damage to the Great Wall Railway and the 75th Railway Section, 070th Railway Defense Forces.
Finally, the Nemertea was eliminated by:
Finally, the Nemertea was eliminated by the 112th Mobile Armored Unit from the 8th Deployment Station at around 14:37. 
This battalion is equipped with three "Typhoon" armored vehicles and two "Coeus" armored vehicles, making it the most elite armed force in the W_2069_0105 area.
According to the unit's report, the main cannon of the "Typhoon" armored vehicles was capable of effectively damaging the Nemertea, and the final kill confirmation was accomplished by one of the "Typhoons."
Post-incident statistics revealed that the armored unit sustained no losses of personnel or dolls.

The stark disparity in casualties shows that the Boojum cannot endure heavy firepower. Considering that other areas in the Yellow Zone are likely to encounter similar high threat level Boojums and that the Railway Defense Forces currently lack the weaponry to address these threats, the following recommendations are proposed:
1. Organizational Adjustments: Reallocate armored battalions from various outpost garrisons into the Railway Defense Forces. Additionally, establish a new fire support battalion to effectively engage similar Boojums.
Additionally, establish a new fire support battalion to effectively engage and inflict significant damage on similar Boojums.
2. Strategic Deployment: When encountering such Boojums, it is recommended to implement the following strategy:
2.1. Disperse the combat engineer company's Dolls to the locations of the Boojum's attacks to avoid concentrated strikes.
Use the automated air defense company and the fire support company's Dolls as the main containment force, with the remaining units held in reserve to avoid wasting manpower.

Report Date: 30 May ██

On April 8 ██, the Monitoring Center began observing and analyzing the behavioral data of Stefan Murnach. Stefan Murnach was selected as one of the observation targets for ███ operations, designated as Subject W/74B.
The subject's behavioral data was observed and analyzed over 405 days. The attention rating was A for the first 240 days and was adjusted to B from day 241 to day 405.
After the attention rating adjustment, the subject's designation was changed from W/74A to W/74B.
The sensitivity rating of the information possessed by this subject is classified as B, covering physical modification treatment plans for E.L.I.D., research on E.L.I.D. incidence rate changes, and clinical treatment experiences related to E.L.I.D.

After 405 days of observation, the Monitoring Center confirmed that the subject did not exhibit any behavior that involved leaking sensitive information.
On May 27, it was confirmed that the subject had ceased all activities, removing the risk of sensitive information leakage. Therefore, the subject was released from monitoring, and the related files were archived and sealed.

May 28, Clear\n\nI sat somewhat dejected:
May 28, Clear

I sat somewhat dejectedly on a chair outside Terysha's bedroom, while AS Val sat beside me, squeezing Teddy.
"How could Miss Terysha become like this... She was so healthy before..."
"Humans in old age have reduced resistance and are naturally more susceptible to Collapse radiation," her teddy bear murmured to itself, "and she's been here too long. This is the frontline of the purification project!"
"So she withdrew all the maids and staff, leaving day-to-day affairs to the Dolls... It seems she must have realized her condition back then!" I recalled Miss Terysha's recent odd behavior and thought, "Her poor appetite lately must also be due to the illness."

Come to think of it, that was also when we were assigned to her room to take care of her daily needs. Before that, we were only responsible for security as bodyguards. Amidst my mixed emotions, I felt somewhat disappointed, especially since I had thought that I was finally getting more attention.
Next to me, AS Val lowered her head even more, her face almost pressed against her teddy bear's chest.
"If only we had noticed sooner..."
I ruffled AS Val's hair to comfort her.

"9A-91, do you know who Herrick is?" AS Val lifted her face, her eyebrows knitted together.
"The name Miss Terysha keeps mentioning when she's delirious? I feel like I've seen it somewhere before..." I searched my neural records, "It seems like this name was written on the back of a photograph..."
The door beside us suddenly opened, and a stern-looking Miss Moran and a grumpy Mr. Durand emerged from the room, both wearing full protective suits. Mr. Durand's somewhat comical voice came from behind his protective mask, grumbling things like, "How stubborn can she be?" and "How could she possibly stay here? She must go back for treatment," as they headed straight for the stairs.

It seems their proposal has been rejected by Miss Terysha once again.
Since her diagnosis, Miss Terysha had become increasingly stubborn—during her lucid moments. When delirious, she would either be hysterical or appear dazed.
The doctor said that her E.L.I.D. had progressed to the middle stage, beginning to affect her mind. If her condition continued to worsen, her lucid periods would become shorter, and she might start experiencing hallucinations.

"Maybe... we could try persuading her? If she doesn't get treated soon, she'll die..."
Honestly, I didn't think Miss Terysha would heed our advice—earlier, when she couldn't eat, we had already suggested she see a doctor. It's understandable—if the employer were to die, AS Val and I might have to find new jobs, and there's no guarantee that the next one will be as stable as this. Besides, I quite liked this lady.

Deep in thought, we dragged our heavy steps into Miss Terysha's room.
28 May, Clear\n\nMiss Terysha laid in be:
28 May, Clear

Miss Terysha laid in bed, without any lipstick on, looking unwell. It felt as if time had accelerated for her, causing her to age rapidly.
Before we could speak, she made a sound; her tone was still elegant and gentle as usual while carrying an undeniable authority.
"I want to go to Clover Garden... please take me to Clover Garden."

AS Val and I exchanged glances. Clover Garden... where was that? From her expression, it seemed AS Val didn't know either.
"Clover Garden... where is it? Is it somewhere in the purification zone?"
Miss Terysha smiled, "It's not in the purification zone; it's in the nearby contamination zone."
The contamination zone? Miss Terysha... she wanted to go there? That's—

Huh?
While I was still considering how to respond, AS Val had already rushed to the bedside. Clutching Teddy tightly to her chest, she made a muffled, distressed weep.
"How could you... You're a middle-stage E.L.I.D. patient. Please be more mindful of it. How could you still want to go to the contamination zone"
"Val...!"

It's rare for her to display such intense emotion. I held down her shoulder, hoping to calm her down, but her anxious expression left me at a loss.
"N-no need to say that. Miss Terysha must have her reason, right? Let's hear her out first."
"Yeah, please calm down. This isn't like you, Val." Teddy's muffled voice came from her chest.
She pouted, her face saying full well she was not convinced.
Miss Terysha smiled as she looked out the window, making her face that was pale as a piece of paper a bit more lively.
"My reason... actually, that's my home. No matter what, I want to see it again... no matter what..."

Val and I exchanged a perplexed glance. Based on our knowledge of our employer, when she said "no matter what," it meant she wouldn't consider any alternatives. A stubborn boss could be quite exasperating...
"Ma'am, do you know the exact coordinates of Clover Garden?"
Weakly shaking her head, Miss Terysha calmly said, "I don't know, but I remember the general direction and route, as well as some landmarks—I remember there was a stone mill with a windmill near Clover Garden."

Taking a middle-stage E.L.I.D. patient to a contamination zone without specific coordinates was extremely dangerous, to the point of insanity. Even with my capabilities as a secret weapon, ensuring Miss Terysha's safety would be a challenge.
But then again, if we could fulfill our employer's wish, that could bring us more attention, right? Opportunities like this are hard to come by... especially after leaving Griffin, where being noticed has become increasingly rare...

"The better option for you is to return to treatment first and go once you have recovered."
AS Val was still trying to persuade her.
"No." Miss Terysha's face which resembled a sketch, turned towards us. "My body is already—"
"Please don't say your body can't hold on," AS Val said, frowning with a serious look. "The doctor said that with active treatment, middle-stage E.L.I.D. is entirely treatable!"
Miss Terysha gave a helpless smile, her expression softening.
"The moment I pass, the purification plan for this area will be immediately cancelled... The construction group will never shift their focus back here again. Even if I recover, company higher-ups will, under the pretext of humanitarian concern, deploy medical staff to monitor my condition at all times, preventing me from ever going to Clover Garden. This is my last chance."
"This is my last chance, it's my request. Please take me home."

I opened my mouth but couldn't find the words to dissuade her. Was there any other way to convince her? I glanced at AS Val beside me and found she was also looking at me.
After a moment of thought, I spoke hesitantly.
"If, Ma'am, I mean if," I turned my gaze to the pale lady lying in the red drapery, "If we take you to Clover Garden, will you immediately return to the White Zone city for treatment upon our safe return? Could you accept our condition—or rather, are you willing to make a promise with us?"
Miss Terysha hardly took a moment to consider; her breath paused for just a second or two before she reached out her right hand to me.
"I promise."

At this point, I bewilderedly gazed at that pale hand.
Although the proposal was mine... I still hadn't truly made up my mind. What if we agree to do so and Miss Terysha ends up dying in the contamination zone? But if I refuse, her stubbornness means she will also die here... Should I gamble on the Group convincing her? Or on us being able to quickly, quietly, and smoothly go to and return from the contamination zone? What should I do? What should I choose?
Damn it! How could I, a secret weapon, be stumped by this?
"Time to take her up on that, 9A-91."
"Val?" I looked at her in confusion, "Weren't you strongly opposed to this moment ago?"
"Because it's... a friend's wish."
Teddy in her arms also mumbled, "I also think it's better to agree. If you're going to gamble, it's more reliable to bet on yourself, right?"
I was startled, thinking that Teddy had some kind of mind-reading function. In my panic, I stepped forward and got tripped over by the bedpost. As I fell, my outstretched hand coincidentally met with Miss Terysha's.

"T-then, let's do it!"
I stood up, cleared my throat, and shook that pale, cold hand of hers, like real business people... well, at least she was a real business person... In any case, we shook hands and sealed the deal.
"Ma'am, please keep your promise. We'll just take a look, and then you'll receive proper treatment once we're back."
I reiterated, attempting to quell the persistent unease.
"Keeping promises is the foundation of being a successful business person."
Miss Terysha answered calmly, her voice steady and firm, just as it was when she issued orders in meetings with others.

This should be the correct choice, right?
As long as we successfully fulfill Miss Terysha's wishes, this stable life will not be interrupted.
With a secret weapon like me, success is guaranteed.
29 May, Clear \n\n\"You sure... this is:
29 May, Clear 

"You sure... this is really okay?" 
"Shh, keep quiet!" 
Just as I lifted my head from the backseat of the jeep, 9A-91, sitting in the driver's seat, pushed me back down. 

In the blinding darkness of the night, only the crescent moon hung overhead, casting down a faint light. I couldn't shake the feeling that it would somehow turn into a sharp sword, slicing my body open and suspending my power core from the tip of its blade. 
I must've been feeling guilty... If I were to keep acting like this, we're definitely going to get caught! 

The purification zone here was still under construction, and the Great Wall Railway had yet to be fully enclosed, thus leaving a gap. The garrison troops had set up a temporary checkpoint, allowing certain personnel to enter and exit the contamination zone through it. We planned to go through this checkpoint in order to gain access to the contamination zone. 
9A-91 drove a jeep we borrowed from the company garage, while Miss Terysha, dressed in a maid's outfit, sat in the back seat with me. She had personally chosen this outfit from the warehouse, along with a lot of portable rations and emergency medicine. She looked like a young girl eager to go on a trip; a stark contrast to the sickly woman who had been quietly lying in bed days prior. 
We also tried using makeup to alter Miss Terysha's appearance to prevent her from being recognized by the garrison soldiers. 

If we were to be identified... we might get immediately caught by Miss Moran. However, neither AS Val nor I had any experience with using these makeups, and Miss Terysha herself only knew how to apply them in a beautiful, elegant, and refined manner. 
After much trial and error, we could only use powdered foundation to somewhat conceal her pores and spots, making her appear more like a Doll. We then applied lipstick to make her mouth look larger than usual and covered her face with a wide hat. 
Although the result was far from perfect, I thought it was fair to consider it a "disguise". 

The jeep came to a stop at the checkpoint, and 9A-91 handed over an ID card. 
"Frontier Construction Group's bodyguard Doll... What's your deal with going to the contamination zone at this hour?" 
Because you'd be busy changing shifts during this period and won't be looking into things too thoroughly... something that I observed when I was on guard by the window. 
"Project manager, Miss Terysha Strelchenko, sent us to survey the nearby contamination zone. We work directly under her." 9A-91 recited the prepared lines, "As you know, we will be assisting with the purification project later, so we need to gather some... uh... relevant environmental information in advance." 
"Environmental information... Tsk, sending a few Dolls to conduct on-site surveys?" 
"This is Miss Terysha's arrangement. Here's the authorization document she prepared." 
9A-91 seemed to be trying to sound more assertive as she handed over a piece of paper. 
The soldier glanced at the signature and seal at the bottom, turned the paper over and over, unable to find any flaws, and threw it back to 9A-91. 
"Any losses incurred in the contamination zone will not be protected by the Railway Garrison. Don't expect us to assist you in case of any danger, understood?" 
She forced a stiff smile, "Of course." 

The flashlight beam swept across the back seat as the soldier demanded that I lower the window. 
I complied, turning slightly to keep Miss Terysha hidden in the shadows. 
"What are you doing? Take off your hat!" 
The soldier reached into the window, pushed me aside aggressively, and directed his flashlight at Miss Terysha. She calmly took off her hat, revealing her pale face, and stared directly at the blinding light. 
"This face looks familiar..." The cold white light flickered over her pale face. 
"Sorry, we're in a hurry," 
Miss Terysha spoke, her voice colder and harsher than usual, "Our employer requires us to return before dawn. You might not understand that lady, but if we cause any delays, she will hold us strictly accountable." 
The soldier with the flashlight frowned and flared his nostrils. "Hmph... Are you threatening me?" 
"Of course not," Miss Terysha said, handing over something wrapped in a handkerchief, "We are asking for your assistance." The soldier weighed the jingling objects in his hand, their yellowish color showing through the handkerchief as they swayed. He sneered and returned to the sentry post. 

The checkpoint gate slowly opened, and I breathed a sigh of relief. Miss Terysha put her hat back on, with her oversized, crimson-colored lips showing beneath the brim, giving a somewhat comical smile. 
"9A-91, were you thinking about calling off the mission if I got recognized?" 
I noticed 9A-91 stiffen noticeably in the rearview mirror. 
"Of course not! I was hoping to use this opportunity to show off and get you to pay more attention to me!" 
"Loosen up, I was just joking." 
"Really... How can you still be in the mood for jokes at a time like this?" 
9A-91 muttered as she started the jeep. Amidst the roar of the engine, I heard Miss Terysha's faint voice. 
"After all, we're about to see Herrick. He doesn't like an atmosphere that's way too tense." 

I was startled, thinking I hadn't heard her correctly, and turned to ask. 
"What did you just say?" 
Miss Terysha's lips were pressed together beneath the brim of her hat, and she didn't answer. 
After a moment of silence, she pulled out a syringe from the supply bag to alleviate her E.L.I.D. symptoms and injected it into her upper arm. I helped her roll up her sleeve and turn sideways to block the jeep window, preventing the soldiers outside from seeing and raising suspicion. 
"...Nothing, let's go." She put away the syringe and closed her eyes, appearing somewhat tired. 
I exchanged glances with 9A-91 in the rearview mirror. She abruptly slammed down the pedal, and the jeep shot forward like a howling Thorn Bear, charging into the contamination zone. 

Actually, I was also thinking that if we were exposed, it might be better to just give up. 
Miss Terysha probably knew that as well.
30 May, Clear \n\nThe ELIDs... there wer:
30 May, Clear 

The ELIDs... there were just too many of them! 
We've been fighting for 2... maybe 3 hours now? Fortunately, we brought plenty of ammunition and fuel when we set out. After all, we were the personal bodyguards of Miss Terysha, so requisitioning more ammunition wasn't a problem for us. However, fuel, food for Miss Terysha, medicines, and protective suits are not so easy to come by... I hoped we could safely return before we ran out of fuel... 
Fortunately, even though I've had a long period of laid-back lifestyle, my skill hasn't deteriorated to the point where I'd be defeated by ELIDs. 

After taking care of a group of ELIDs surrounding the jeep, we decided to take a break for a while. 
9A-91 and I returned to the back seat and administered a drug to alleviate Miss Terysha's mental symptoms. 9A-91 clumsily broke off a piece of compressed biscuit and placed it in her hand. 
After passing the checkpoint, Miss Terysha changed into her protective suit. However, after several delusional struggles and delirious attempts to jump out of the car, the suit became damaged, so we had to use sealing tapes for temporary fixes. The visor was in a sorry state, smeared with dirt, sand, saliva, and the lipstick from her mouth. 
It has been 5 hours since we departed, and Miss Terysha's moments of clarity are becoming increasingly brief... 
At this moment, she was very quiet after the injection, awkwardly attempting to lift the visor of her protective suit but kept failing due to the effects of the medication. 
I helped her lift the visor. She thanked me with a smile and stuffed the biscuit into her mouth. 

"We're running low on food." 9A-91 said, rummaging through the supply bag on the seat, "The medicine as well." Indeed, we should have been better prepared. However, postponing all this might've made everything worse with Miss Terysha's condition... Agreeing with Miss Terysha's request was indeed imprudent... 
I sighed silently while 9A-91 spoke very softly: "Miss Terysha, based on your recollection, it should only take about 3 hours to travel from the purification zone to Clover Garden... If we fail to locate the place by dawn, we'll have to return back, or Miss Moran will certainly discover that you're missing from your room." 
I nodded in agreement and looked at Miss Terysha. It was only then that I noticed her eyes were sparkling and her cheeks were flushed with vitality. 
"We'll find it," she said, brushing off the crumbs from her hands, "Don't worry, we'll definitely find it." 

9A-91 and I exchanged a bemused glance. 
"To be honest... Ma'am, I do not share your confidence... Please consider the possibility that we might not find it, and..." I carefully chose my words, hesitating over whether to ask the question that had been troubling me for a long time. 
"Why do you insist on visiting your old home? I don't understand. If it's to visit your family, there might not even be anyone living there anymore, right?" 
"Teddy...!" 
I quickly covered Teddy's speaker, and the car fell into an awkward silence. Neither 9A-91 nor I blamed Teddy, as he had asked the question we were all thinking. 

Miss Terysha stared at her reflection in the car window. 
"Herrick actually loved sweets." She broke off another piece of the compressed biscuit, "Whenever he finds something sweet, he can't help but take a secret bite first and then pretend to be innocent if caught." 
"Uh, Ma'am, though I've asked before... who is Herrick?" I asked hesitantly, unsure if she would answer this time. 
"He is my elder brother," Miss Terysha smiled, her expression was youthful like that a teenage girl, "There were eight children living in Clover Garden, all of us found—or rather, picked up—by Herrick, like pulling radishes out of a hole, he brought us home." 
She chuckled softly, resting her chin in her hand, her eyes sparkling as if reminiscing about the past. 

"Every year he had to prepare eight birthday gifts, which really gave him a headache, especially when we could barely afford to eat." 
"So, when I heard that news, I thought I could at least give him a birthday present to make him happy," her eyes grew dim, "But... he didn't like my gift." 
Miss Terysha seemed a bit tired and closed her eyes. 
"Let's go east, we'll definitely make it back." 
I gave 9A-91 a puzzled look, and she gently shook her head. "We couldn't understand how what Miss Terysha related to her determination to go back to Clover Garden." 

There was no time to think. 9A-91 tapped my shoulder and pointed to the rearview mirror. 
"Wh—...!" 
I saw reflected light in the rearview mirror—not starlight, but the glow of the eyes of ELIDs. 
"Time to go, AS Val." 9A-91 jumped out of the car and hopped back into the driver's seat, while I opened the window and fired at the ELIDs that were already within range. 
Amidst the roar of the engine and the gunfire, I heard a voice that was so faint that it was almost imperceptible. 
"I also prepared a gift for you two, it's in my office terminal. Check it out when you get back. If you don't like it, that's fine. The password is written in the notebook on the top shelf of the left cabinet." 
"A gift?" 
I turned to look at Miss Terysha in her seat. She didn't answer my question, still resting her chin in her hand with her eyes closed, as if she had fallen asleep. 

The jeep, pursued by shadows, sped away from the moonlight.
30 May, Clear\n\nAs the moon gradually s:
30 May, Clear

As the moon gradually set, the jeep made a coughing sound and we lost engine power.
At this moment, only one of our headlights was still shining forward, faintly revealing the outline of a dilapidated mill. Above the mill, two of its four blades were stubbornly turning in the wind.
I heard the rear door open and saw Miss Terysha had already jumped out of the car and fallen to the ground. Despite the Collapse crystals protruding from her pale, fragile skin, she continued to struggle and crawl towards the ruins.
I shot down an ELID lunging at her, and AS Val immediately ran over to help her up. In the distance, familiar glimmers of light were gathering— We had seen them countless times tonight already; the eyes of ELIDs.

AS Val patted her face and handed Miss Terysha to me, then climbed onto the roof with her gun.
"9A-91, you go ahead. The destination... it's right there. I'll hold them off, you take Miss Terysha."
I was silent for a moment, glanced at our employer beside me, and then looked up at AS Val. "You'll be alright, won't you?"
She patted Teddy and flashed me a wide smile.
"Of course... Don't forget, I'm the best there is when it comes to night battles. Miss Terysha... I'll leave you with my friend."

I carried Miss Terysha and ran towards the dilapidated house. In the thick darkness, the outline of the jeep quickly faded from view.

Next to the windmill, as jagged as an old man's teeth, a small ruin of a house lay silently in the deepest darkness before dawn.
There were no clovers in this "Cloverfield"; it was just a dilapidated house with a wooden sign nailed to the door, featuring a simple sketch of a clover.
The roof had likely been gone for a long time. The walls were barely standing, consisting of a few planks that looked they might fall over at any moment and signs that the place had been set on fire at some point. Miraculously, some items in the house were still intact.

I kicked a box on the ground to make sure it was stable, then helped Miss Terysha sit on it and found a candle stub on the floor.
I lit the candle, which faintly illuminated the interior. It was only then that I noticed Miss Terysha was sitting opposite a broken mirror, which seemed to be the remnants of a dressing table. Her reflection in the mirror showed her aged and somewhat disheveled face.

"Miss Terysha, this should be the place, right?"
She didn't answer right away. Instead, she frowned as she stared at her reflection in the mirror. She looked somewhat puzzled as she reached out to wipe the dust from the mirror and traced the reflection of her face with her fingers.
Watching her in silence, I also fell silent, remaining vigilant of our surroundings.

The room still showed some signs of life, but it had undoubtedly been abandoned long ago. If this was indeed Miss Terysha's home, her family must have... The ground outside the house appeared uneven, possibly hiding something buried there?
But who could have buried it...?
"Ah!"
"What's wrong?!" I was jolted out of my drifting thoughts by her sudden shout.
"How rude of me, how could I let a guest stand?" Miss Terysha stood up unsteadily, pressed on my shoulder, and made me sit on the box.
"Wait a moment, I'll get you some water." Before I could react, she stumbled over to the other side of the room. There had been a cupboard there once, but now only a few planks remain of it.
"The cups should be here... Ah, this is Morac's cup! Will this do for you?"
She mimed a searching motion through a non-existent cupboard.
"Morac?"
"Oh, he's my younger brother, buried next to the windmill."
"Buried...?"
I couldn't parse her words right away.

"Yes, he encountered a Mishap Thorn while foraging outside. When Herrick found him, only a part of his calf was left, still wearing the socks I had sewn for him... (Sigh) He was ill back then and too thin, there was no way he could have escaped." There was a hint of sorrow in Miss Terysha's tone, but it was mostly one of resigned acceptance.
"After that, it was just me, Herrick, and Tral left here again."
"Three of you? You mentioned there were eight children... did the others all..."
"Yes, either attacked by ELIDs or suffered from chronic malnutrition... It was hard for children to grow up here, and even if they do, they ended up with E.L.I.D. Hmm, wearing this makes it hard to pour water."
I quickly rushed over to grab her hands as I saw her trying to remove her protective gloves. I couldn't bring myself to look into that dirty face shield.
Although I always knew that life in the contaminated zone was very difficult, actually seeing it in the flesh made me feel... sad.
Wait! Now was not the time for sadness. There was something off about Miss Terysha just now. It would seem her E.L.I.D. got worse in the contaminated zones. We had to take her back quickly.

"Miss Terysha, we must go, if we stay here any longer—"
"Tral, you think they're pitiful too, don't you?"
"Huh?!"
Miss Terysha cupped my face with her gloved hands, lifting my head slightly.
Her face was close, displaying a tender and radiant smile. The eyes behind the mask sparkled with youthful light, gazing intently at my face.
"Ah... I didn't mean..."
"It's okay." She spun in place; if she had been wearing her usual soft, silky dress, the hem would have fluttered.
"When I graduate, I'll change this place!"
"Graduate? Isn't this a contaminated zone? Is there... a school here?"

"Unfortunately, I haven't heard of any schools in the contaminated zone. The school I'm talking about is in the Green Zone!" She had a hopeful look on her face. "It's a newly established school. It was originally meant for children in the Green Zone. However, due to insufficient enrollment, they're willing to accept students from the contaminated zones, provided they pass a medical exam and an entrance test. I just saw the exam results— I passed! I can go to school!"
The words kept flowing out of her. I'd never seen Miss Terysha like this.
"Once I get to the Green Zone and settle down, I'll find a way to bring you over, so you won't end up like the others. You're so frail. And Herrick won't have to..."
Her expression dimmed.
"Herrick... what happened to him?" I tentatively asked.
"Herrick disagreed with me about going to school." Miss Terysha sat back on the broken box, resting her chin in her hand. "I thought it was good news and that he'd be happy... but he thought those schools were a political ploy to lure more people to the Green Zone and control them... He said that even if I went to school, I wouldn't be able to change anything."
"But... isn't it better than waiting to die here?!"
She leaned forward, holding my hands as if seeking my approval.
"Yes, today I'll talk to him again. This time, I won't argue with him. But even if he disagrees, I will still..."

"Tral! Won't you come with me? If Herrick doesn't agree, I'll take you with me even if I have to knock him out!" Miss Terysha's voice suddenly grew excited. She stood up, hugged me tightly, and rested her chin on my head.
In a panic, I blurted out.
"Miss Terysha, I'm not Tral!"
She released me and stared at my face again. Her brow furrowed and the look on her face grew increasingly confused and serious as the girlish expression on her face faded away.
"So it's you, 9A-91... I see, it seems I mistook you for someone else."
She held her forehead, swaying slightly. I held her by the shoulders.
"We need to go back, Miss Terysha."
She was silent for a moment, then nodded calmly at me.
"Alright, you go out and wait. I need a rest... and to freshen up."
"But you can't remove the mask..." I grabbed her hand as she turned towards the mirror.
Miss Terysha gently patted my fingers gripping her wrist, then held my hands, shaking her head softly. She smiled tenderly.
"It's alright, 9A-91, it's... alright, don't worry."

I stared at her in a daze.
Her face quickly went pale, her lips turning ashen. I realized I had been staring at my employer for too long, so I quickly looked away and pulled my hand away, speaking in a voice so low I could barely hear it myself.
"Please... limit your exposure to environments with ambient Collapse radiation."

"Okay." She replied.
Miss Terysha tidied her tattered protective suit, walked over to the broken mirror, then lifted her mask, and took out her lipstick, applying it carefully. After confirming her makeup was in order, she put her mask back on, walked over to the bed that was so worn and dust-covered it was unrecognizable, and lay down.
"Alright, 9A-91, leave me alone for a while, I want to rest."
Through the filthy mask, I saw her face, as pale as paper, with her crimson lips forming a faint smile. I walked out of the room, my footsteps feeling heavier than ever.

"9A-91, it's living here that made me the person I am." Miss Terysha crossed her legs so she could lie down more comfortably. "What will you become?"
"I... we—" We are Dolls, all we can do is follow our programming. That was what I wanted to say, but when I opened my mouth, the words wouldn't come out. In the end, I instead said, "We'll wait for you outside."
Surely that was not the answer she wanted to hear, yet Miss Terysha still wore a radiant smile as she lay on the bed.
The sun appeared to be rising, warm rays streaming through the gaps in the walls, reflecting a shimmering glow on her face.
"There's no rush. Think about it carefully, 9A-91, you have plenty of time."
She closed her eyes.

I walked out of the room and closed the door.
The wooden sign engraved with a clover tumbled to the ground, rolling away in the wind with a clattering sound, resembling a stumbling, aimless drifter lost in the vast contaminated zone. As I watched the sign roll further away, it felt as if I could hear Miss Terysha's steadfast voice asking me once more.
"What will you become?"

In the dim light, the jeep in the distance cast a long shadow across the dusky yellow ground. From the roof, AS Val waved at me, holding Teddy up.
I lifted my hand, trying to return the smile, but my stiff lips refused to budge.
What will we become?
...I'll ask AS Val too.

As the sun rose, I walked towards the jeep.
