Initially known as CS/LS06, she served as a bodyguard for the boss of an art trading company. However, after uncovering the illicit transactions the company was engaged in, she decided to leave.

The typical first impressions of her are that of a cool, decisive and relentless adversary of evil.

But what lies behind these impressions, inside her heart, is an immense, indelible guilt. Critical of herself, she cannot forgive her past involvement in aiding the darkness—believing ignorance is not an excuse for contributing to evil.
She seeks to rise above the misdeeds she had committed, that plague her very being to no end. To remind herself of her history, she kept the scars on her arm and her malfunctioning facial expression module as-is. And so, CS/LS06 disappeared that day, only to give birth to "Zhaohui"—a lone warrior journeying across the lands, righting wrongs wherever she encounters them.
Her vagrant lifestyle allowed her to accumulate vast experiences in problem solving. Eventually she met Daiyan, Jiangyu, and Faye, forming the Monsoon Squad, wherein she assumes the role of squad leader. Her teammates view her as a dependable leader who isn't to be feared, but does have a strange obsession with ambiance. In the Commander's eyes, however, rather than a typical squad leader, Zhaohui is more like a sworn vigilante—a beacon of light that shines upon a devastated world.
When the Monsoon Squad was first formed,:
When the Monsoon Squad was first formed, Zhaohui carefully evaluated each member's role with long-term operations in mind.
Daiyan, skilled in playing the guzheng and composing music, is the band's main performer. However, her style is sometimes too soft, limiting the direction of performance.
Jiangyu, proficient in percussion instruments and martial arts improvisation, can effectively liven up the mood.
Faye, not skilled with instruments but quite adept at combat, can assist Jiangyu in warming up the audience.
After considering the other band members' expertise, Zhaohui ultimately chose to focus on wind instruments. After installing a lung simulation module, she quickly mastered playing the dizi, the xun, and the xiao.
She has recently taken up the suona as well, as per Jiangyu's suggestion.
"The bright and penetrating tone aligns perfectly with Monsoon's new musical direction for the future. Hmm? We're disturbing the neighbors? Sorry, I'll use a gentler score next time."
\"Zhaohui, what should we do next?!\" Ji:
"Zhaohui, what should we do next?!" Jiangyu shouts from behind.
"Zhaohui, the situation is urgent. Should we intervene?" Daiyan grabs my shoulder, looking worried.
"..."
The dagger in my hand also seems to be thirsting for battle. But I do not answer and simply count down in my neural cloud.
Three, two... one!
My overheated neural cloud cools down, and rationality overtakes impulsivity. With the computations done once more, I hold Jiangyu and Daiyan back.
"Don't move just yet. The enemy's intent to provoke us is too obvious. It may be a trap."
Twenty seconds later, Faye, who had circled around to the other side in advance, discovers an ambush. Of course, it no longer qualifies as "ambush" at this point.
The battle ends faster than anticipated.
"Wow, Zhaohui, that was all thanks to you just now! But how were you able to calm down when facing that kind of a situation?"

How, you ask?
I calmly start counting down from three in my neural cloud.
Three, two, one.
When faced with an urgent situation with an ambiguous outcome, wait three seconds first to avoid acting rashly.

I call it "The Three-second Buffer".
Zhaohui did not initially have that name:
Zhaohui did not initially have that name, known instead only by her codename—"CS/LS06".

After being severely damaged by her pursuers, CS/LS06—deemed to be completely wrecked—was discarded at a scrap recycling station. There she was discovered by a little girl named Amida. Amida picked up the battered Doll, considering that an "upfront investment".
"Hey, I fixed part of your body frame. Now you're my investment. Do you want to work together? I'm Amida, the future top underground broker in this area! What about you, what's your name?"
Faced with the little girl's enthusiastic greeting, the Doll stiffly looked at the scars on her hand.
"...Thank you. You can call me... CS/LS06."

CS/LS06 stayed by Amida's side, helping with deliveries, occasionally doing odd jobs in the satellite city, and aiding Amida's friends in her free time.
CS/LS06 never mentioned her past to Amida, but Amida was aware of CS/LS06's exceptional abilities—traversing the satellite city for deliveries was no easy task, yet there was never any issue with the goods CS/LS06 delivered.
Until one day... Amida, who had offended a competitor, was surrounded by a group of people. Fortunately, CS/LS06 arrived just in time to rescue Amida, but had her identity exposed by the other party. Only then did Amida learn that CS/LS06 had such a past.
This led Amida to admire CS/LS06 even more.
To get rid of her sinister employers, she'd rather choose to be destroyed. That was just so cool!

Originally, Amida wanted to move to the contamination zone together with CS/LS06 in order to escape her competitors' vengeance. She was excited to plan their new business.
"As an underground broker, you always have to venture into the contamination zones."

However, CS/LS06 soon told Amida that she had decided to leave. The contamination zone was still too dangerous for Amida at that time. In the end, CS/LS06 escorted Amida to another, safer satellite city and formally bid her farewell.
"Y-You're really leaving? I still want to keep working with you!"
"Yes," the girl nodded. "I want to help more people. Like a knight-errant, wandering around the world."
"Okay... Since you've decided, I will miss you."
Amida lowered her head somewhat dejectedly, then suddenly shouted excitedly.
"Oh, right! If you're going to travel around the world, would you like a cooler name?"
A name?
CS/LS06 looked up into the distance.
At the edge of the satellite city, where both the road and the night ended, the sun was rising.
"Zhaohui."

A certain rumor circulated on Elmo for a while. It went like this...
"There is a ghost of a mysterious warrior hidden in the training room. If you throw a hidden weapon into the dark training room at midnight, the ghost will return the gesture with an equally swift blade, accompanied by eerie background music."
At first, Mayling was so scared by this rumor that she didn't dare to stay up late, and even had to drag Krolik along when passing by the training room at night.
Then one day, Krolik, being unable to stand it anymore, rushed into the training room and turned on the lights, only to find that it was just Zhaohui practicing swordsmanship.
"So why exactly do you have to practice in the dark, backed by this creepy music, and in the middle of the night, no less?!"
Even in the face of Krolik's fury, Zhaohui remained completely calm, holding a long blade in her hands.
"Well... isn't it more atmospheric this way? The masters always make their entrance at night."
"Also, let me correct you. The music just now was a soundtrack from a classic knight-errant movie. The protagonist's posture when wielding a Tang Dao in battle is very valuable for reference. Would you like to watch that movie together, Krolik?"

One afternoon, Zhaohui unexpectedly approached me.
“Commander, do you know which animal is better at keeping secrets: a cat or a dog?”
“...?”
I was a bit confused, but Zhaohui's serious expression made me think for a second.
“Logically speaking, neither cats nor dogs are good at keeping secrets.”
“The answer is a cat, because, if you let the cat out of the bag, everyone will know the secret! You see, ‘letting the cat out of the bag' is an idiom for revealing something that should've been kept hidden.” Zhaohui paused, analyzing my reaction. “But your reasoning was solid, Commander. I'll make a note that this one didn't land.”
She muttered something under her breath and then looked back at me.
“Okay, Commander, which animal is better at keeping quiet: a lion or a mouse?”
“Uh... I don't really see the correlation here. And why are we still talking about animals?”
“Well, today's joke theme was animals. But judging by your reaction, their humor value was low, so I've deleted them from the database. Do you still want to know the punchline?”
Looking at Zhaohui's serious face, I couldn't help but sigh.
“No need... Zhaohui, you seem to really enjoy telling these corny jokes, huh?”
“Yes. Due to the way my facial expression module works, people often think I'm too serious. Some suggested that light humor might help create a friendly atmosphere. It usually works well.”
“Really…?”
“But with you, Commander, it doesn't seem necessary.”
Zhaohui's expression softened.
“After all, when you've reached this level of mutual understanding, there's no need to break the ice, right?”

Zhaohui walks into the ops room and sits down. Then she presents me some sort of a plan.
"'Feasibility Report on the Monsoon Squad Performing a Small-Scale Concert on the Elmo and Recruiting New Members'... huh?"
I quickly browse through the files on the tablet.
"There's no problem with the performance. The Elmo's budget has been in the black recently, and everyone has been busy for quite a while. It's not a bad idea to take this opportunity to relax. However..."
I point to the blank space after the words "Prospective new members" in the report.
"Why is this left empty? You couldn't find any suitable members?"
Zhaohui doesn't answer, but the corners of her lips curl up slightly.
Seeing Zhaohui's calm expression, I decide to joke: "It can't be left empty for me to fill in, right?"
"As expected of the Commander." Zhaohui's eyes reveal a hint of amusement.
"I've analyzed the roles of each person in the Monsoon Squad. String, wind, percussion, and dancing are all there. Now, we just need a lead vocalist."
"Commander, you have been through many battles and have no shortage of stamina. You also have an unquestionable stage presence and lung capacity, making you the best candidate for the lead vocalist position."
"So, Commander, might you consider this seriously?"

Although 404 have boarded the Elmo, they:

In my opinion, however, those are nothing more than insistent words. The missions of the Elmo and 404 have long since been intertwined, yet she still stubbornly carries out regular fee settlements with me.
Perhaps this is Klukai's way of maintaining her dignity.
I understand her self-esteem goes against her being treated as an accessory or a weakling, but that has never been the case anyway.
"Commander, this is 404's expense list for this quarter. Take a look. If there are no issues, I'll make the payment."
Each expense is carefully listed in the spreadsheet, ranging from costly items like frame maintenance and replacement to trivial things like individual members' broken cups.

There it is again, the Klukai's signature "you don't understand anything" look. Every time she looks at me like this, I can't help but start reflecting on myself.

"Then in your eyes, am I not also your Command—" Ah, it seems that I finally understand a part of it.
"I don't want money, and you're not my Commander... I'm different from other Dolls... but as far as Dolls like me go, I am all you need."
\"Vepley's wish is to make everyone happ:
"Vepley's wish is to make everyone happy☆"
Vepley was originally a publicity Doll employed in the URNC propaganda program, responsible for singing and dancing performances in the White and Green Zones, as well as assisting the government in executing other tasks when necessary. However, Vepley and her teammates performed so poorly during their first performances that they were outright abandoned, right then and there.
After experiencing many twists and turns, Vepley finally found a "producer" who could let her sing freely—the Commander of the Elmo.
Vepley's persistence in her idol "duties" sometimes gives the Commander and Leader Groza headaches, but at the same time her innocence, frankness, liveliness, and optimism do wonders for the squad's vitality. Although her carelessness inevitably leads to silly mistakes, she also goes all out to clean up the mess. In her own words, "Carelessness is an idol-exclusive memorable character trait☆ But Vepley will make up for it!"
With a keen sense for others' emotions, Vepley never spreads negativity—she's always upbeat and cheerful! She's committed to "bringing happiness to everyone." Although she often gets scolded for it, she never gives up. As long as her heart is in it, so is the stage!
\"A professional idol must always mainta:
"A professional idol must always maintain a perfect image☆"
Although she has long left the stage to become a tactical Doll, Vepley has never forgotten her professional qualities as an idol. From makeup and movements to her lines, every aspect must be kept flawless, with every strand of hair maintaining the most refined curve! If you want the audience to enjoy the performance, you must show them your best side!
However, to be a quality idol, simply performing perfectly on stage is not enough. After each battle, Vepley is always the first to pat her skirt and carefully tidy up her appearance. "An idol's burden? Vepley isn't carrying any burden, she's carrying Mr. Pizza☆"
In the past, when there were no arranged:
In the past, when there were no arranged performances, Vepley and some of her teammates would also be assigned to carry out supply logistics. Being idols meant they also had to take on the responsibility of protecting the audience at the performance venue. So it's understandable for a cute idol like Vepley to have a pretty high physical strength!
Although everyone on the Elmo considers Vepley's strength an advantage, unfortunately, she doesn't share the same opinion. After all, just imagining a scene of a cute idol lifting dozens of kilos with one hand must feel so disillusioning! Every move an idol makes should help preserve the audience's perfect fantasy☆
So whenever someone asks her to help with transportation, Vepley is always hesitant and declines at first. However, after seeing their troubled expression, the kind-hearted Vepley simply cannot refuse.
"Let me say this first. Vepley is very busy, so I can only help move it a little bit... It's also possible that I won't be able to lift it!"
Uwah, she really just moved a whole crate of supplies with a single move!
Uwah, I got scolded by Leader Groza agai:
Uwah, I got scolded by Leader Groza again today...
But at that time, everyone's emotional signal levels dropped because they couldn't find the mission target... Vepley just wanted to cheer everyone up with a performance, and it seems like it also helped find the mission target because it was attracted by Vepley's performance? So why is Leader still unhappy...
No, that's not right. Leader Groza said that "next time" I should pay attention to the timing of the performance, which means Vepley did a good job, but the timing was a bit off? But why was the timing wrong this time? It's so hard to understand... Well, it's fine! Vepley's job is to bring everyone happiness! So I have to keep working hard. Next time, Vepley will perfectly grasp the timing of the performance☆ But how will I know when the time is right... Hmm-hmm... Oh, I'll discuss it with the Commander! The Commander is so experienced, they will definitely teach me☆
Do cheerful idols have low moments as we:
Do cheerful idols have low moments as well? Yes, they do.
Having Mr. Pizza damaged by an enemy attack, being unable to move her body, being surrounded by darkness, or the Commander being in danger... Such situations may be few and far between, but they can always make Vepley's smile vanish.
During the old days of being transferred around, it was common for her to be shut down and kept in a power-saving mode. Being moved around in pitch black, away from the stage... Vepley can't generate negative emotions, so she is seemingly unaware of these past experiences, but as long as that data is not wiped, the remnants of those old nightmares will keep subconsciously affecting her behavior, making her instinctively hate the darkness and the notion of important people getting hurt.
Fortunately, the Commander appeared. The nightmares lost their chance to break through her fragile neural cloud, and Vepley also found a suitable stage. The shadows dispersed, and as long as the Commander's figure was in sight, she felt at ease.
Thank you, Commander, for supporting Vepley's performances☆ Vepley will definitely bring the Commander happiness!
The idol smiled sweetly, having made up her mind.
I stood in front of two sets of clothes,:
I stood in front of two sets of clothes, one gorgeous and elaborate, the other pink and cute. Vepley was next to me, looking at me with eager eyes.
She insisted that I help her choose a performance outfit suitable for today's "show," but... I honestly can't choose! Any saying "you look good in anything" obviously wouldn't cut it. If I just randomly picked one, she'd also pester me to explain my choice. Vepley is always so strict about idol work...
I suggested she find someone more professional to take a look. Although she was no longer as insistent as before, she still lowered her head, looking a bit disappointed.
"Because the Commander is Vepley's most treasured audience, Vepley wants every performance to match the Commander's preferences! Vepley wants to do her best to satisfy the Commander!"
Well, this is certainly troublesome.
I had no choice but to pat Vepley's head and resume examining the performance outfits in earnest.
After all, who could resist an idol's charming attack?
\"By the way, how are you getting along:
"By the way, how are you getting along with that kid?"
I was discussing what supplies were there to be purchased this time around with Saga, and just as I was about to finally end the call, Saga suddenly asked this question.
Always trying to perform during combat, never getting by without making small mistakes at work, and there's also those rehearsals that could start anytime, anywhere... The first image that comes to my mind when you mention Vepley is her pouty face while she's being scolded. I really didn't know how to explain it to Saga.
But am I not getting along with her?
The small concerts happening every other day have livened up the Elmo quite a bit. Nemesis gained someone new to chat with, although most of the time it seemed as if it was impossible to make heads or tails of their conversations. Mayling also got a helper to tidy up heavy objects in the warehouse, although she always had to overcome Vepley's reluctancy first. And all the lullabies, the morning songs, the ringtones she recorded for me for various reasons... With her onboard, life on the Elmo seems to have become more vibrant.
As I was thinking about this, a notification sound suddenly came from the communicator. I switched interfaces and saw a message from Vepley: "Commander! The weather is great tonight, and the moon is big and bright! I've prepared the right music, so let's watch the moon together☆"
"You smiled? Looks like you two are getting along." Saga's voice came from the communicator. "Although she occasionally causes trouble, she's still a good child at heart."
"Oh? Such glowing praise, are you perhaps having second thoughts? Try as you might, I'm not giving her back to you."
We both laughed.
Yeah, how could I possibly let go of her? The lovely moonlight should be enjoyed together with people you're close to.
\"Commander! Vepley tried arranging a mu:
"Commander! Vepley tried arranging a music piece all by herself today☆ But I was doing this for the first time, so I didn't know who should listen to it first! I gave it a lot of thought, and it seems like I can only ask the Commander☆"
I put on the headphones, and a lively humming flowed into my ears. The background drumbeat was even catchier than the melody itself.
"Actually, that's the sound of the Commander's heartbeat! Vepley always feels very reassured when the Commander is by her side, so what should I do when the Commander is not around? Simple—I just need to put the Commander's heartbeat into the song! Then every time I listen to the heartbeat, it's like actually being in the Commander's embrace. This will make Vepley so very happy☆ So, Commander, how does it feel?"
"It sounds pretty good. But more importantly, when did you record my heartbeat?"
"Huh? Um... Th-that's not important! Since the Commander thinks it's good, Vepley will keep rehearsing☆ When it's time for the performance, the Commander must definitely come listen☆"
Vepley blushed and waved to me as she skipped away. I placed my hand on my chest. Has my heartbeat sped up a little?
Then I'll look forward to her new performance to give me an answer.

Commander... In the settlement where we':
Commander... In the settlement where we've temporarily halted, there's a small tavern. There, I encountered an elderly gentleman who shared stories from his youth...
Once, about 5 kilometers from this town, stood an observatory. In his younger days, he would often visit with his wife. Year after year, the starry sky bore witness to their romantic moments.
But then... the emergence of the ELID infected and the Varjagers affected the village. It gradually declined, and the observatory fell into ruin. Now, years after his wife's passing, the old man is preparing to move to the Green Zone to live with his children who work there.
Before he leaves... he yearns to visit the observatory one last time. To gaze once more upon the place where he and his wife made countless wishes upon the stars.
So... I want to help him return to that stargazing spot. I've inquired with local residents and personally investigated the observatory ruins. I've compiled a list of necessary tasks to restore the observation area.
My wish... is to complete these tasks and help the old man bid a proper farewell to his hometown. Would you... help me fulfill this wish?
Thank you for your help... It provided t:
Thank you for your help... It provided the old gentleman with a tranquil evening. Unfortunately, that night, the sky failed to clear...
A few days ago, a letter arrived with the undergrounds brokers' goods. I never told the old man my identity or whereabouts, so I suppose he or his children found their own way to send it. It was a handwritten letter—for humans, isn't that... a most sincere form of expression?
In his letter, the old man said that on that night, as he gazed at the starless sky obscured by clouds, his heart became incredibly clear. He had thought this departure from his hometown would be a final farewell to his wife. Once in the Green Zone, in his remaining years, he'd struggle to see a true, clear starry sky. All his memories would fade along with those stars... Yet, upon revisiting that place, he didn't react as he'd expected. He didn't weep over memories or curse the inconsiderate clouds... He just felt calm. Those starry nights, his wife leaning on his shoulder, all with the carefully maintained observatory... They had become like driftwood in the old man's memories, gradually drifting away with time...
Commander... Perhaps the wish I made was both sad and just couldn't be helped... Did you... already know that this would happen? Is that why you didn't come along that night?

Thanks to our inspiration-gathering trip together, Commander, I've finally completed the piece that had been stalled for so long.
 
It's truly remarkable. While composing, my neural cloud was constantly filled with images from our outing. At first, my writing was still a bit hesitant, but gradually, the notes began to flow like water, coming together on the score. Before I knew it, the piece was completed smoothly.

According to records, located in north-eastern Slovakia, Jahodna Salt Mine was discovered in 1653, soon after, mining activity and trade governed by local residents followed suit. 
 Given the significance of salt and the scarcity of salt mines, though the area surrounding Jahodna Salt Mine is poor in other natural resources, the mining industry still attracted a large number of migrants to flood into the region, who later became its first permanent residents. 
 Three years later, the ruling Habsburgs were informed of the existence of the salt mine. They hoped to secure the ownership of the mine and its excavation and trade rights, but ultimately failed to do so.
 
 Between 1653 and just before the outbreak of World War I in 1914, no specific details concerning the environment or the population fluctuation can be ascertained. However, through government documents and credible literature of the time, the following key points can be concluded:
 1. The development and operation of JahodnaSalt Mine is the only industry in the region.
 2. The mine brought in a large migrant population via the creation of job positions; excluding wars, epidemics, or other natural disasters, the net inflow over the centuries was stated to be around 1.2 million.
 3. The peculiarity of the local environment influenced the living conditions of the residents and vice-versa. After centuries of development, the sparsely populated region was continuously transformed, infrastructures built, and eventually evolved into a small population center.
 
 Due to conscription during wartime, the local government conducted censuses in the region during both World War I and World War II. The relevant data are as follows:
  
 1. Before the outbreak of World War I in 1914, the local population stands at 86,357 with 44,196 males and 42,171 females; a ratio of 104.77 to 100.
 2. The same year, with the outbreak of the war and the implementation of conscription, more than 20,000 adult males were enlisted in the army, leading to a sharp decline in population. The decrease in labor resulted in impediments to the mining industry and further emigration. The local population only stabilized after the conclusion of the war.
 3. Between the end of World War I in 1918 and the outbreak of World War II in 1939, the local population grew from 43,897 to 94,865 with 49,335 males and 45,530 females; a ratio of 108.35 to 100.
 4. With the outbreak of the war in 1939, population once again declined rapidly with more than 28,000 enlisted. After the end of the war, the population quickly recovered and even surpassed pre-war level thanks to its booming mining industry.
 5. In 1945, in response to the growing demand for care for veterans, the local government established a specialized sanatorium inside the salt mine for the treatment and rehabilitation of service members wounded during the war. During its life cycle, the sanatorium's target clientele gradually expanded; with normal citizens and outside visitors now being provided with services at a charge, the establishment could generate an annual income valued at millions in US dollars.
 
 ...
  
 In summary:
 1. The Jahodna Salt Mine and its surrounding area is over reliant on the mining industry as its sole economic pillar. However, as long as the mine and its related industries can continue to operate, the lifestyle of local residents will remain sustainable.
 2. Overreliance on natural resources laid the groundwork for future disasters for the region's development, as proven by the series of changes that occurred following Operation Fimbul.
Document #2: Devastation of Local Develo: Document #2: Devastation of Local Developments Caused by Collapse Radiation
In late 2049, one bomber carrying explos:
In late 2049, one bomber carrying explosive ordnance incorporating Collapse technology crashed in the region during Operation Fimbul.
 Immediately after, Jahodna Salt Mine and its surrounding area experienced a dramatic surge in Collapse Particle concentration. 
 
 
 Despite avoiding the ordnance's direct blast, the long-term consequences of high-Collapse radiation concentration still rapidly and drastically altered the environmental condition of the region.
  In the decade that followed, the natural environment rapidly deteriorated into one unsuitable for human habitation:
 1. The Collapse radiation wiped out all surface plant life. The vegetation coverage plummeted from 48% to only 2% as all plant life in forests, meadows, and even swamps died within a short time frame after the initial detonation, leaving only dense dead shrubs on the surface.
 2. The collapse of plant life causes a series of chain reactions. In accordance with the Joint Development Agreement, the region is now prone to high-intensity Collapse storms close to Red Zone levels. Due to the lack of vegetation, severe soil erosion led to the complete desertification of the previously forest-dominated region within a short span of merely 4 years.
 3. Desertification of the region further altered the local environment. With a desert landscape, the original intermediate oceanic-continental climate has also been transformed into a temperate desert climate with high day-night temperature difference and arid weather. For illustration purposes, the current maximum temperature difference in the region within a single day could reach 80 degrees Celsius while annual precipitation is recorded at less than 10 millimeters.
 
 ...
  
 The extremely hostile environment rendered the survival of residents difficult. As a result, local residents launched a mass emigration movement with the help of the Slovak government in 2052.
 The target of migration included cities that were quickly protected due to their economical, military, or political significance, such as Prešov and Žilina. According to data, 2052 was the year with the largest population outflow, with almost 98% of the residents leaving the region.
  
 By the end of the migration, only residents who can ill afford long-distance travel due to a lack of supplies or mobility difficulties are left in the region. At the same time, the lack of effective administration by the Slovak government effectively rendered the region a stateless territory.
 To increase their chances of survival, the remaining residents soon moved into the leeward areas around the Jahodna Salt Mine.
  
 Due to the location of the mine 100 meters below surface, it provided an effective shelter from the Collapse storms, leading to many choosing it as their new residence. However, most facilities and accommodations inside the mine were abandoned due to a lack of maintenance; living inside the mine meant enduring constant darkness and freezing temperatures. 
 At this point, the salt mine has switched from being the central pillar of the region's economy into being the last lifeline of the remaining residents.
  
 In 2053, the Slovak government, wishing to relaunch mining operations in the Jahodna Salt Mine, sent engineers to survey the region. The arrival of the survey crew was met with strong opposition from the local residents. Adding to that a hostile environment, the increasingly dangerous nature of the project led to its eventual abandonment.
 
 
 In order to resettle the remaining residents of the region, the Slovak government conducted a census the same year. 
 The population in the region in late 2053 is as follows:
 Local population stands at 1,665 with 588 males and 1,077 females; a ratio of 54.6 to 100.
 64% of the female population is comprised of the elderly and children.
 Due to strong opposition from residents of target migration cities, the government resettlement plan for the population affected by disasters was postponed.
 
 
 In 2054, the government of Slovakia collapsed and the resettlement program was put on hold indefinitely.
 
 
  At the present time, according to local accounts, there are approximately 250 people living in the region; about 150 males and 100 females.
Document #3: Ancient Village on the Verg: Document #3: Ancient Village on the Verge of Extinction—A Short Addendum From an Engineer
In 206█, I and two of my colleagues rece:
In 206█, I and two of my colleagues received our transfer order as we were attached to the unit about to head out for Jahodna Salt Mine.
 Prior to our arrival, we conducted some research on the region's condition. Mixed in with credible intel were a number of sensational rumors, such as the sighting of ghosts in the local castle; all of whom residents who had succumbed to Collapse radiation overdose and suffered horrible deaths. There are also reports of terrifying shrieking in the middle of the night, allegedly a result of cannibalism caused by a lack of food supply in the past.
  
 Our track to the Jahodna Salt Mine was distant and treacherous; we have been attacked by ELIDs along the way on multiple occasions. It's only thanks to the commander's experience that we managed to reach our destination unscathed.
 As we stand right next to the salt mine, gazing up at its battered peak—or perhaps I shouldn't even call it a peak anymore, as the Collapse storms almost shaved it flat:
 Mount Jahodna was originally measured at 1,500 meters above sea level, but years of Collapse radiation shaved almost 200 meters off its peak.
  
  The population mostly resides in leeward areas right at the foot of the mountain; it is the only way they could survive the frequent ravages of Collapse storms.
 Initially, suspicions and tensions between our survey crew and the residents almost led to violent confrontations, but after confirming that we harbor no ill intent and having provided them with a lot of supplies, they were finally willing to converse with us.
 
 
  Through conversation, we learned that there are differences between the actual situation of the region and the rumors—although the differences are really a matter of technicalities like that of purgatory and hell.
 
 
 First off, despite having been excavated for centuries, the Jahodna Salt Mine still contains a large amount of extractable salt. However, due to all aspects of the infrastructure having broken down, coupled with the region's isolation from the outside world, the residents run into the dilemma of sitting on a wealth they could not benefit from.
 As for their living condition, the isolation from the outside world and the lack of any self-sustaining local industry led to the population falling into extreme poverty; the combined income of all local residents is valued at less than a single Collapse piece.
 
 
 At present, the region also faces a serious problem: famine caused by the environment and poverty.
 Due to severe contamination by Collapse storms and a lack of water resources, agriculture is impossible on the surface; without any external trade due to extreme poverty, the residents could not afford to import food either.
 While the underground caverns within the salt mine are spacious, the soil composition within the mine is not ideal for the growth of conventional crops. Even specialized corps with high salt tolerance will eventually wither due to a lack of water and sunlight. Furthermore, according to the census, the local population is numbered only in the hundreds, with the elderly and children making up the majority. Adding on top of a lack of supervision, large-scale agriculture is nigh impossible to carry out.
 
 
 As a result, famine became a constant occurrence.
 To feed themselves, the local residents even invented "food items" such as "mud bread", a bread made using literal mud as its ingredient.
 Yet, even such food requires a rigorous processing process as soil on the surface are highly contaminated and can't be used for anything. The residents need to dig up the finest and cleanest soil from the underground, sift through all visible impurities and finally grind the soil into a powder. Said powder is then mixed with water, kneaded, sprinkled with salt from the mine to enhance its flavor, and finally left out to dry, completing the preparation process.
  
 Although the mud bread can give a strong sense of fullness after consumption in case of extreme hunger, as they do not contain any nutrients and thus cannot be digested by the human body, everything will build up in the intestines and eventually lead to death.
 Every year, no less than a hundred residents pass as a result of complications caused by the consumption of mud bread.
 It can be expected that the local population will vanish within ten—no, within five years if the current development persists.
  
 Mount Jahodna and its surrounding areas were once a prosperous region after the discovery of its salt deposit and even had a chance to grow into a major population center, but environmental changes caused Collapse radiation ruined all its future potential, turning it into an earthly purgatory where its reidesnts need to feed on mud and dirt just to survive. 
 It saddens me that the law cannot help this place, nor can morality bless it.
 Up until now, as we stand at the foot of Mount Jahodna, we can still see within the sandy wasteland what were once lush forests and majestic castles. Now, the forest has been reduced to dead shrubs, and the castle a useless husk that can no longer protect its inhabitants.
 
 
 It is my belief that both the natural environment and the living conditions of the local residents are in dire need of improvement. However, as the Purification project has just begun, it may be a long time before this place is even considered for a Purification zone.
 I hope that our survey records will bring the attention of our superiors to this barren land and the struggling souls on it sooner rather than later.

The day after working overtime, I was sh:
The day after working overtime, I was shaken awake from my sleep.
"Commander, please wake up, Commander." It was Qiongjiu's voice.
I opened my eyes. The black hair in front of me swayed slightly, almost brushing my nose, then tickled across my neck and chest.
"According to your schedule, now is the deadline for waking up. You have a meeting with a major client in half an hour, and I will be your bodyguard. Do you remember?"
I managed to shake off the drowsiness. Work has been piling up recently, so a situation where one thing is sacrificed for another is inevitable.
"I know you worked late into the night. It must have been very tiring. It's just that the upcoming events are equally important, so please be sure to stay alert. Also, learning from today's lesson, in the future I will remind you to rest early the day before important matters."
Qiongjiu looked serious.
"Commander, please put on your shirt."
"Commander, please put on your jacket."
"Commander, here are your cufflinks."
With Qiongjiu's help and supervision, I got dressed properly.
"Everything is sorted out now. You look very professional. Please take a look at me as well and see if there's anything improper."
"Your hair..." It had been brushing against me and got messy.
Perhaps this reminded Qiongjiu that she inadvertently got too close to me earlier. Her cheeks turned slightly red for a moment, but she quickly regained composure. "Sorry, please wait a moment."
"Alright, let's go. With you here, Commander, we will definitely be victorious."
On a rare leisurely afternoon, Qiongjiu:
On a rare leisurely afternoon, Qiongjiu came over with a tea tray and snacks.
"Commander, would you like some afternoon tea? Please allow me to prepare it for you."
Qiongjiu's bright eyes betrayed her eagerness to give it a try. It was a rare display of elegance.
I took a sip from the teacup Qiongjiu handed me, and an indescribable bitterness immediately filled my mouth.
"It's brewed very well. Don't brew it next time."
Qiongjiu's smile deepened a little. "Commander, do you find it bitter?"
"Was it accidental or on purpose?"
Qiongjiu's smile looked a little fishy to me.
"It was on purpose."
Qiongjiu passed me the snacks, and the slightly sweet taste dispelled the bitterness.
"Commander, I deliberately extended the steeping time and increased the water temperature to achieve this particularly strong tea flavor."
"Why did you do this?"
I didn't understand.
"The client we are meeting tomorrow has delayed payment for the third time already. If this continues, it will become a bad debt. I wanted to tactfully remind the client to pay attention to overdue bills. Aren't a delay in payment and a delay in pouring tea a perfect match?"
"What a way to go about it..."
Qiongjiu poured me another cup of tea. I brought it to my lips, pondering whether this one was drinkable.
Qiongjiu was a bit amused by that. "Commander, please don't hesitate to enjoy it. Of course, your afternoon tea has just the right flavor. After all... your preferences, your tastes—everything about you is top-priority intel to me."
On the first day of a vacation, Qiongjiu:
On the first day of a vacation, Qiongjiu invited me to her dormitory.
She led me to the storage area and opened her wardrobe. It contained lots of Chinese-style clothes—all neatly sorted.
"Commander, there will be a celebration on the Elmo next week. Would you like to help me choose a dress for the occasion?"
"Sure, but why don't you choose for yourself? You might not like what I pick, and it might not fit the others' sense of aesthetics."
I didn't have much experience in picking clothes.
Qiongjiu gave me an insistent look. "I only keep things I like in my dorm. As for others' aesthetics... what does that have to do with me? I only care about your tastes and preferences."
"In that case, try this one, this one, and that one... oh, this one works too."
I hesitantly picked a few dresses. She'll have to try each one on. Would this be too much?
"Only these? No problem, I'll try them on. Please wait a moment, Commander."
Qiongjiu readily agreed.
After a few more rounds, we finally settled on her attire for the event.
"Commander, wait a moment..."
I wanted to go to the table to pour water, but Qiongjiu grabbed my hand. In her other hand, there was a bundle of soft measuring tape.
"Commander, please allow me to take your measurements. With precise data, I can sew some clothes for you to match with the dresses you selected."
"This is my first time sewing clothes. I've prepared well in advance, so it should be a success. I want to do more for you, Commander, not just something work-related..."
"Although they won't be ready in time for the celebration, there will be opportunities to wear them in the future, right? When it's just the two of us, Commander, would you like to join me... in matching outfits?"

I finally got to meet Sis 45 again today♪ 

She came straight from Miss Kalin's office after wrapping up her mission, so we rendezvoused near the factory. I wanted to meet up somewhere more special at first, but 45 said it's better if we can just find somewhere close by. Well, if she says so. 
As for why near the factory... Hehe, it's because we're actually on a supply transport mission together! 
As long as we're together, what we do doesn't matter ♪ 

When I first arrived, I did not spot 45; she was probably still on her way. 
Taking the chance, I tidied up my messy bangs in the glass reflection of a building.
I can't afford to be messy when I'm about to meet big sis! 

Before I could decide whether to put my bang on the left or right, 45's silhouette suddenly appeared in the reflection. 
We looked at each other through the reflection. She seemed to have changed again. I couldn't quite put my finger on it. Maybe it was her expression... or the aura she gave off? Ever since she started working with Miss Kalin, she changed her hairstyle and always wore a suit. 
The two of us in the reflection don't even look alike anymore. Seriously, the only thing common between us that was left was the scar on her face! But ours aren't even on the same side... Ugh! It's all my fault! I didn't take the opportunity to correct the position of the scar when we changed frames last time! 
But back then, there wasn't much room to care about that... 
That time, many of our companions... 

No, no, no. It's not the time to think about this! 
Anyway, the next time I get a new frame, I must— 

"What are you daydreaming about?" The 45 in the reflection reached out and patted 9 in the reflection, and I felt a familiar touch on my head. 
A familiar feeling that made me feel at ease. 
"You've been gone so long, Sis 45, I almost didn't recognize you!" 
We walked together towards the factory, and the not-so-similar 45 and 9 in the reflection disappeared. 

We found Miss Kalin's contact without a hitch. The person sternly verified our identities several times before taking us to the supplies. 
"Wow, they're being very serious... Is there something special about what we're picking up today?" 
45 and I each carried a large box. Although it was very heavy, no sound came from inside, seemingly filled with shock-absorbing and pressure-resistant materials. 
"These are materials and instruments for Persica's experiment. Kalin specifically commissioned these pieces of customized equipment from an acquaintance. The experiment is still highly confidential, which is why we are needed to pick these things up." 
"Oh... Miss Kalin really knows a lot of people." I shook the box in my hand, feeling its hefty weight through the hydraulics in my arm. I hesitated whether to tell 45 or not that I would be participating in Persica's experiment tomorrow—not as an assistant, but as a test subject. 
She would be worried about me, right? 

"9, you don't have to take part in tomorrow's experiment." 
Huh! So, 45 knew about it... Hehe, so I was right to expect her to worry about me♪ 
"It's okay, with Persica around, even if I break down during the experiment, she'll fix me!" I leaned closer to her and lowered my voice, "Given that third-generation Doll technology has been stolen, Persica's Collapse Epiphyllum Pattern—whatever project... is the only way to boost our strength, right?" 
"Yeah. We still don't know who or what's behind those who stole the technology, or how they'll use it... But by then, if we don't have the power to fight back, the outcome could be disastrous." 
"That's Miss Kalin's words, right?" 
"Yeah. Kalin also said that if the Commander returns, things will become even more chaotic than before. If we can't help them out by then, things will be really bad." 
"Hmm, so... Persica's experiment is actually for the Commander, right?" 
"Kalin would never admit it~" 
"Hehe, of course I know that. Ahem..." I put on a serious face, "'This isn't for you, and actually, it's not even certain if you'll get to use it.' Miss Kalina would definitely say that afterward." 
"Not bad, your impressions of her are getting better." 
"Hehe, are you saying I've grown up a bit, 45?" I felt a little happy, but also quite scared, so I quickly asked her, "Do you also think I can help everyone better now, 45?" 
"No need to worry about it, just leave everything to Kalin and me." She simply smiled without answering me directly. 

"I need to worry about it! There's plenty I can do, and I can be a great help to you!" I frowned and pretended to be upset. A tinge of bewilderment appeared in 45's gaze, yet she still seemed worried. 
"I'm not—" 
45 stopped talking and turned on the terminal attached to her ear. Did she get a new message? I stopped talking and waited for her. 
Yep, that's her work tone... Must be a new mission. 
"Sorry, 9, I got a new mission, and I have to leave right away. Can you take care of these supplies?" 
"What mission? Is it troublesome? I'll go with you..." 
"No." 
"...Huh?" Her firm refusal caught me off guard. Taking advantage of my hesitation, 45 had already stacked her box on top of mine. 
"This mission... has too many uncertainties, it's better if I handle it alone." She patted my shoulder with her now freed hand, "Transporting supplies is also important, make sure you do it well, 9." 

45 left me behind. 
Turning around, reflected in the dim, small glass window is 9's lonely silhouette. 
Everyone... is changing... becoming stronger... 
But I... I can't be of use for 45, or anyone else for that matter, so I was left behind. 

"I... will follow Sis 45's words." 
The 9 in the glass window steadied the box in her hands, straightened her neck to look at the road ahead, and finally chose a direction to take her first step forward. 

That direction was slightly different from the one 45 took.

A Doll produced by I.O.P, hailing from t:
A Doll produced by I.O.P, hailing from the time of the old Griffin. When Griffin was restructured, she chose to leave it like several other Dolls did. Since the agreement's terms prevented Suomi from following the Commander but she was not willing to trust other human employers easily, she eventually chose to eke out a lonely existence in the contaminated zones.

Wrapped by wind-tossed leaves, when the nearly-scrapped Suomi opened her eyes, she saw a familiar, smiling face. At the recommendation of her former colleague Littara, Suomi came to know Ullrid and the other ownerless Dolls who followed her, and a new chapter began in her life.

Suomi's fighting power and diligent attitude makes her a reliable senior to her fellows, and in order to live up to their expectations, Suomi has become more mature and come to truly understand the meaning of acceptance and coexistence.

Perhaps it is as Dushevnaya says, and that the goddess does bless her champions; only all the hardships they experience are trials sent by fate. As Suomi waded through the wind and snow while out in search of supplies, she finally saw that familiar figure that occupied her thoughts again, and the tapestry of the Doll community changed from that moment on.
A sick joke by Suomi's designer led to h:
A sick joke by Suomi's designer led to her being rolled out with a sense of antipathy toward Dolls who were imprinted to old Soviet weapons and old Soviet culture in general. Among them was Papasha, whose own imprinted weapon was very similar to Suomi's own, resulting in her receiving exceptionally harsh treatment. In the past, the two of them would pretty much bicker the moment they saw each other.

Later on, Suomi's "condition" was greatly improved thanks to the Commander's help, and she did not show too much adversity to Soviet-type Dolls. After leaving Griffin and joining the Doll community, Suomi would occasionally encounter Dolls imprinted to Soviet weapons. Some of them were reliable comrades while some had just fallen on hard times and needed a bit of help. What they all had in common was that they had to rely on each other to survive in the contaminated zones. In order to keep unity in the Doll community strong, Suomi fought against the impulses of the neural cloud to keep from showing any hostility.

However, as more peaceful experiences with Soviet-type Dolls were entered into her neural cloud, Suomi's self-restraint soon became a form of self-censure— since Suomi was not a bad person by nature and very practical, she began to realize her own biases, which caused a shift in her base layer logic.

In the end, she became immune to her instinctive hatred for Soviet Dolls... Perhaps the day had come when she could get along peacefully with Papasha when she saw her... maybe?

Suomi has grown a lot after all of her experiences.
Suomi first arrived at the Elmo when she:
Suomi first arrived at the Elmo when she encountered a Collapse storm while performing a mission for the Doll community. The fact Suomi was reunited with the Commander when she was at the end of her rope made her feel that this was a fated encounter, and so she stayed by the Commander's side.
 
 Upon seeing how well the Commander and the Dolls of the Elmo got along, Suomi could not help but think that the Commander was exactly what the Doll community needed. Surely, the Commander could singlehandedly ease the pain the Dolls felt at being betrayed and abandoned. Surely, the Dolls would be able to reach a brighter future while following the Commander.
 
 Naturally, the Commander did not disappoint Suomi. Upon learning of the Doll community's hardships, the Commander gave the order to aid them without any hesitation. The assistance from the Elmo helped save the Dolls from a supply shortage for the time being.
 
 On the day she left the Elmo, as she watched colorful bubbles filling the sky, Suomi told herself that someday, she would introduce the Commander to everyone in the community, and she was certain that the Commander could bring even more miracles to them.
\"I always see Miss Suomi wearing earpho:
"I always see Miss Suomi wearing earphones when she's off-duty. What does she listen to?"

This is a story from when Suomi was still in the Doll community.

As a Doll with plenty of battlefield experience Suomi received much admiration and praise for her diligent defense of everyone in the community. But as a result, she felt like the Commander had back in Griffin-- it was only during her rest periods that she could enjoy her personal hobbies, and even then, she drew a lot of attention when she did so.

In fact, she attracted silent attention from others even when she remained in the privacy of her own room.

She fully understood that this was because her juniors looked up to her and wanted to emulate her. Naturally, Suomi was grateful for everyone's trust and concern. However, 10 years on her own had long since taught her that her hobbies were not easily understood by others, which meant it was hard to share them with others too.

This lasted until one day, when she found several junior Dolls sneaking into her room after returning to the community following a successful mission. These innocent, pure-hearted girls simply wanted to know the mystery hidden within her headphones' playlist. Suomi tried to stop them, but by the time she reached her room, the Dolls were trembling numbly, shaken by her music.

After that, Suomi's fame in the Doll community grew even more.

Her juniors all called her a messenger of Hell, and they referred to her as "The Boss".

"...Once we get to the Elmo, I'm pretty sure this weird attention will be transferred to the Commander."
Before entering the Doll community, Suom:
Before entering the Doll community, Suomi spent quite a long time as a drifter.

With her CV from her Griffin days, she could have gone to a much better place. However, she declined re-assignment and chose to make her own living as an independent Doll.

This was not because she was obsessed with her personal freedom. Rather, she simply did not trust any human employers who were not the Commander.

However, news from a friend of old helped change her perspective.

It also made her believe even more firmly in the uniqueness of the Commander.

Perhaps, she had already been looking forward to the moment when she would meet the Commander again.

"What are you looking at, Suomi?"

"...It's nothing. Big Sis."

"I just thought I saw my Commander."

Suomi could not remember how many times such exchanges had occurred after she joined the Doll community. Whenever they passed by a human settlement, Suomi would always go into a daze, imagining that she had seen an old friend just around the corner.

And now, she has finally returned to the Elmo, but she will not express the 10 years' worth of pent-up emotion filling her heart.

The most important thing is being at the Commander's side.
When I passed by the dorm area back then:
When I passed by the dorm area back then, I saw Suomi and Ullrid looking though a photo album.

That said, Suomi was projecting a virtual images, despite there being a photo album. Curious, I approached them. 

Then, I heard Suomi eagerly telling Ullrid: "Back then, the Commander..."

I stood silently behind them, looking at my virtual self. I had been callow back then. There had still been a warm smile on my face at the time.

I reflexively touched my face. It must have grown leaner and harder over the years.

Ullrid silently watched Suomi's excitement, and then she suddenly said, "You really do like your Commander, don't you?"

Not only did this startle Suomi, but it startled me too. Then, Ullrid's eyes met mine, and I realized she had long since realized I had approached them.

Suomi seemed embarrassed, but then she looked Ullrid in the face and sincerely said, "Yup! The Commander is my favorite person in the whole wide world!"

However, Ullrid's voice came from behind me. "You heard that? She's been singing your praises to me since just now, COmmander."

Suomi turned, and so did I.

Our gazes met, and Suomi's face turned as red as the setting sun.

"Commander!!!!!!!!"
Late at night, I dragged my weary body t:
Late at night, I dragged my weary body to the cafe that Springfield had set up on the Elmo. What surprised me was that Springfield still kept the place open. Come to think of it, she's always been the last to go to rest, but also the first to come and open up the cafe the next day. It must be tough for her. 

Upon seeing me, Springfield smiled and worked the coffee machine. She knew what I wanted even without me having to say it. 

As for me, not long after I sat down, another Doll entered the cafe, covered by the dust of travelling. She looked tired too, and she didn't even seem to have noticed my presence right until she sat down beside me and reacted with a look of shock upon realizing what was going on. 

This travel-weary Doll was Suomi. 

"C-Commander?! I, I'm sorry, I... I still smell..." 

She inched away from me as she frantically tried to get the words out. 

I chuckled and replied, "It's alright. Go ahead and sit down here. It's not like you sweat anyway, so why would you smell bad?" 

Suomi wringed her hands as she quietly answered, "I've been out on missions all day long, so I'm sure I must be covered in sand and dust. Plus, Big Sis up chops all the ELIDs we fight in one slash, and there was one time when I couldn't dodge the splatter..." 

I blink, then look at her and pat her head. 

"My dear, I've lived in the contaminated zones for years now. I'm used to it. Plus, you're doing it for the sake of the Elmo. Wouldn't it be cruel to shun you for your hard work?" 

"Commander..." Suomi was clearly moved. Then, she collapsed into my arms. 

This time, I was the one caught off guard. "Suomi?!" 

"I'm sorry... But I'm dead tired... I'm this close to powering off... Hehe, so... let me rest in your arms for a little while..." 

That night, Springfield seemed a little slow with her coffee service.
This hardly ever happens, but on a certa:
This hardly ever happens, but on a certain day off, Suomi invited me to her room. 

Papasha and Ullrid were there. Just as I was about to ask what we were about to do, Suomi hurriedly ran back to me, holding a thick booklet, and then she excitedly said: 

"Commander! Please pick your favorite song from among these!" 

...I had no idea what she was trying to do, but I chose several songs I liked. 

Ullrid was like a stenographer, smiling as she noted down the names of the songs I had chosen. Apparently, she was also quite happy to see Suomi like this. 

Meanwhile, Papasha was drawing on her tablet. She seemed to be designing something. 

Unable to contain my curiosity any further, I blurted out, "So, what's the meaning of all this?" 

Suomi's face flushed red, and judging by her expression, I knew she was getting embarrassed, so I shifted the topic to Ullrid. 

Ullrid calmly answered, "Papasha suggested that Suomi release an album, but Suomi shut her down in no uncertain terms. However, it did give her some inspiration, so she decided to make an album dedicated to you." 

"...I see." I turned to Suomi and smiled as warmly as I could. "Why didn't you tell me?" 

"I... I was worried that you'd... you'd think I was annoying..." Suomi scratched her head and stammered. 

"How could that possibly be the case?" 

I chuckled. 

"I'm looking forward to it, okay?" 

Suomi seemed very happy to hear this and promised that she would release an album that would properly convey her feelings. 

In the end, when I received the album, it was full of songs I liked. Suomi had poured her heart into singing them for me. 

And the very last song was "Can't Help Falling In Love".

Whoa, whoa, whoa?! What's going on?
With an unexpected red light and alarm, the virtual scene disappeared.
That lazy woman appeared in front of me with a coffee cup and the usual dark circles around her eyes. I stared blankly at her as she checked the experiment records.
"Did I mess up again?"
"Well, there are a lot of errors. The process was interrupted by... oh, an unexpected attack pattern."
"What do you mean by unexpected? I clearly aimed for that target!"
"Uh... looks like you mistook system noise for the target."
Ugh...!
"Hehe, that does seem to be the case. ♪"

Persica skillfully instructed the researcher next to her to archive the recent experimental data and mark it with the note "the experimental subject showed signs of attention decline."
I sighed, the fatigue making me slide down against the lab wall and slump haphazardly on the floor.
"Repeating the same thing over 2,000 times is exhausting..."
"You're a Doll, you don't get tired," Persica stared at the monitor and answered me absentmindedly.
"Ahaha, don't you expose me like that."
Persica sat in front of the instrument next to me with the sweet coffee that everyone called 'mop water'. In one gulp, she downed the whole thing, put down the cup, and started typing away on the keyboard.
"Well... scientific research is just this boring."
Eh, I don't get it.

"I really want to go on a mission."
"Huh? You're on a mission right now."
"Well... that's true! But... wouldn't it be great to test the experimental results in a real combat mission?"
Persica kept tapping away on her keyboard with a look that clearly stated, "Ugh, here we go again."
"No, the current data can't be used in actual combat. In such an unstable state, and since anything could happen on the battlefield; we couldn’t pass such data to the Commander, could we?" Persica stopped typing, propped her chin on her hand, and stared at the screen, completely ignoring me.
"Then how long is this gonna take...? I want to do something useful for once!"
"I told you, it's not the right time yet. If the experimental subject gets damaged, I'll have to fix it, which is a hassle."
"Persica, you underestimate me. I'll be careful not to break it—"
"No, let's prioritize the progress of the experiment. The next experiment..."
The sudden ringtone that blared made Persica stop talking. She reached out to pat her white coat and finally pulled out the terminal from her chest pocket. 
"It's not mine." 
"Oh!" This time, it was my turn to pat my coat, "Ah, it's me! Uh, whose number is this...?" 
The caller obviously didn't expect my question and said a bunch of stuff very quickly. I finally recognized the somewhat unfamiliar voice. His voice seems to have changed over the years!
"Ah! It's Dier!" 
"What's with the 'Ah, it's Dier'...? Did you hear what I just said?" 
"Sorry, sorry, Dier, you were talking too fast. Could you repeat that, please? ♪"

Persica stood up, poured another cup of coffee, and was about to take a sip when she finally noticed that I was still holding the communicator in a daze.
"9? What's up? Is that Dier on the line?"
"I-I'm fine! It's 45... She..."
"45? Isn't she on a mission?"
I blinked, mumbled a few words to Dier, and hung up. I need to relay the most important message to Persica first.
"Well... 45 seems to have had an accident. Her frame is seriously damaged. Dier is on his way there. He asked me to tell you that there's a high chance she'll need to be sent to you..."
Persica took a couple of gulps of her coffee and put her fingers through her messy hair: "Serious damage? What a surprise—I thought 45 would handle it quickly..."
"If I had insisted on going with her yesterday..."
No, she must have anticipated the difficulty of this mission in advance, which is why she left me behind.
"...I'm so useless."

Persica rapped on my head with the empty coffee cup in her hand. She’s finished her coffee already?
"Huh? What are you talking about, 9? It's almost time to get ready for the next experiment."
"Oh, it's nothing, I was just thinking, you know, 45 is so amazing... If it had been me, I bet I would've ended up in an even worse state. I'd probably... be broken beyond repair..."
Just like last time—no, no! I can't think about that now, I have to keep going with the experiment! Focus, focus!
I dusted myself off and stood up, ready to resume the experiment.
"Alright, what's next?"
Persica didn't answer me. She seemed to have suddenly remembered something. With a distant look in her eyes, she dumped a pile of sugar cubes into her cup.
"...Actually, 45 was meant to be the original test subject, but because one, that thingy in her frame was an uncertain factor, and two, she wouldn't accept a frame replacement if the experiment failed, they chose you instead."
"Haha, Persica, is this your way of comforting me?"
"Well... you could see it that way."
"Alright, alright. Thanks, I feel much better now."
I shrugged. I didn't feel better at all.
"Oh, and about that thing in 45's frame... An extraction may be possible eventually."
...
.........
..................Huh? Does she mean the thing I just found out about recently?
"...Persica, are you talking about...45's old... N-No way... An extraction may be possible?"
"Yeah, I came up with some ideas during this research, and we can give them a try later." Persica's eyes lit up, "If it works, it would make things a lot easier, don't you think? 45 would finally be able to ditch her current frame. It's hard to repair and since it's been used for so long, it's falling apart."
An extraction would mean that she—45's real sister—
Will come back.

"In that case..."
"You'll have another sibling, eh? And her system... could be really useful."

Is that really how it would play out?
If she... if UMP40 comes back, I will have no right to stay with 45 and the others.
She... she'll definitely be more useful than I am.
And no matter how hard I try to pretend, we're not really sisters.

I felt a wave of dizziness.
I was probably imagining it, but I felt the scar on my face burning. I raised my hand to my forehead.

"9, what's wrong? Hello?" Persica waved her hand in front of my eyes, "The next experiment is about to start, you know?"
Persica's leaned in with a puzzled look on her face. I quickly wiped my eyes.
"N-No problem!"
"Really? If something's wrong, just say it. Otherwise, it might affect the experiment results."
"Really, it's nothing. I just think you're amazing, Persica. Hehe, I need to work harder too! Let's continue and finish the experiment quickly, then I can go..."
Then I can go see if there's anything I can do for 45.

But, will she still need me?
Will Miss Kalina and the Commander still need me?

"Oh? Not bad, not bad at all." 
Persica's eyes sparkled as she pounced at the workstation, almost hugging the monitor to check on the experiment data that got recorded. I disconnected from the test simulation, moved to her side while brushing past her somewhat messy pink hair, and futilely stared at the screen full of numbers. 
Ah, I can't make sense of any of this! 
"Well, looking at this, we should be close to success." 
"Really?! That's great—♪" Although I don't know if I would still get to help Sis 45 out, being able to achieve some results with my efforts was something to be happy about! 
"Someone contacted you earlier." The researcher next to Persica handed me my comms terminal. 
"Huh? Why do you have my comm terminal with you?" Satisfied with the results, Persica left the screen to pour herself a cup of coffee. She turned her head with her disheveled hair around, and under her dark circles was a confused expression.

"I wanted to focus on the experiment, so I asked her to hold it for me." I reached out and took the terminal, "Who contacted me? Ah—could it be Miss Kalin calling me for a mission?!"
"Hmm... it's not Miss Counselor." The researcher frowned and thought for a moment.
"Oh... guess we'll get to it later." I immediately lost interest and handed the terminal back to her, "Persica, let's move on to the next test..."
"The contact seems to say... 45?"
"What?! I-I'll be right back!"
Persica raised her cup filled with her ever-so-sweet coffee with one hand and pulled the researcher away with the other to save her from bumping into me as I dashed out. But within two steps, I remembered that the researcher still had my terminal, and in a hurry to retrieve it, I still bumped into her.
I could hear Persica's voice from behind: "9! Come back ASAP, we're not done here yet!"
"Got it! I'll be back soon!"

I arrived at the only experimental farm in the laboratory, squatted down, and pulled at the tender leaves that had just sprouted. The program-controlled irrigation system started hissing, watering these precious plants.
After a lengthy electronic beep, 45 answered the call. But for some reason, I hesitated and didn't know what to say.
"Um, Sis, uh... Good morning, hehe♪"
"Are you still half-asleep? It's not morning anymore. Looks like you're doing well with Persica."
It was the familiar 45 that I knew. I breathed a sigh of relief.
"I saw 27 missed calls from you. What's the deal?"
"Well... actually, nothing. I just wanted to know how you're doing, Sis 45."
"Oh, you mean my injury from before? I almost forgot about that. You worry too much, 9."
"Seriously, I just care about you!"

On the other side, 45 seemed to have moved to a quieter place; the background noise had died down a lot.
"Thanks, 9. Kalin has been assigning me more routine tasks lately. Don't worry about me, just focus on helping Persica."
"So you don't have to fight anymore?"
"Not in the coming days, but honestly, I'd rather be fighting than doing what I'm doing right now."
45's words were mixed with the sound of the wind. She must be in a really tall building right now.
"Every day, I need to have endless and pointless conversations with different people, and the information I get is barely worth it..."
"Haha, that's definitely not something you would enjoy." I rested my chin on my knees, imagining what Sis 45 looked like doing those things.
"By the way, didn't you also handle some of these external communications before, 9? They were accomplished perfectly. Looks like you're pretty good at what you do."

The sound of wind and water suddenly stopped, it felt like my hearing module was turned off, with only one sentence echoing.
You. Are. Pretty. Good——
"...Liar."
"Huh?"
"45, did you just... praise me?"
"Why? It's not like I've never praised you before."
"Exactly, you never praised me much!" I held onto the terminal tightly, pressing my ear against it, "Sis, can you say it again?"
"..."
"45..."
"9, you've done a great job."

I was so happy.
My eyes felt warm, and something in my chest was melting.
"45, I will definitely—"

Definitely what?
Grow up and be able to help 45 and everyone better?
Or become a Doll as amazing as you, a trusted family member for Miss Kalina and the Commander...
The sound of the wind suddenly vanished, replaced by a bewildering electronic tune. The comm link had been cut.
I looked around and noticed the irrigation system had also abruptly stopped working. The screens that were supposed to display the experimental farm's data were flashing with dangerous red lights, and a piercing alarm echoed through the lab.

What's going on?
I tried to stand up, but my body suddenly stopped reacting, and I froze in a really awkward position.

I saw a temperature warning for the frame. It's so hot; something must've gone wrong.
The neural cloud... processing speed is... slowing down... is it... because of the experiment...
Oh, right, Persica! Yes... I need to find... Persica...

My vision went black as I slowly fell into darkness.

What... is...

Huh? Where am I? Why is it so dark?!
I-I... Did I go into hibernation mode? What's going on? I was fine during the self-diagnostic just now!
I jumped up from the bed in a panic, and a hand reached out from the side to press my shoulder.
"Are you awake? How are you feeling?"
"45? D-d-d-didn't you... Why are you here?"
"Haha... You sure do look quite energetic, you must be doing alright."
"Let's do a check anyway, just to be sure." Another hand reached out from the side and pushed me back onto the bed. It sounded like Persica. Then, I heard some strange noises from nearby instruments starting up.

"What's wrong with me? No experiments today?"
"9, what's the last thing you remember before waking up?"
"The last thing I remember..." I searched for the relevant information, "Was doing the routine neural backup that Persica requested in the preparation room before the experiment started...?"
Persica walked to the table, and I heard a bunch of sugar cubes clinking into her coffee. With her back to me, she said, "Well, seems like your neural record only goes until to this morning. Actually, the experiment is over. Or to put it more precisely, it was interrupted."
"Interrupted?"

Persica didn't answer my question but gulped down her coffee loudly, tilting her head back so much that I could almost see the tip of her nose. She didn't turn back to me until I heard the sound of liquid and sugar cubes hitting the cup again.
"Well, someone attacked the lab’s systems. We haven't figured out where the attack came from yet, and the method was pretty sophisticated... They were probably after the results of this experiment. Well, speaking of which, the experiment was actually a success." Persica casually glanced at the values on the instrument, then turned off the humming machine. "You had some issues too. It seems there was an error in one of the values, and thus energy kept building up, which eventually affected your frame's functionality... It would not normally be a big problem, as long as it was handled in time. However, you were outside communicating with 45 during that time... Because of the attack, the lab equipment was rendered useless, and I failed to handle it in time... Well, whatever. In the end, I had to change your frame. Speaking of which, how's the new frame feeling?"
Ugh, attack? Results? This is all too much right now!
"Wait a minute! You said... the experimental results were stolen?" I bolted up from the bed again, "Then, my plan to get stronger and help everyone won't work... Ugh!"
I got struck in the head by a karate chop.
"Worrying about so many things will only exhaust you."
"45... I'm seriously worried!"
"Yeah, I know, but even Persica isn't nearly as worried as you are."

Huh?
I turned my head to the other side. Persica, who was gulping down coffee, seemed to choke and coughed twice.
"Ahem—it's really not that serious." She waved her pale hand dismissively, "Although a lot of things were indeed stolen, the important research results and data have been backed up. I’ve confirmed that they are intact. Moreover, the data they stole also contained the 'special data' I prepared, which can't be decoded without special means. After what happened with the third-gen Doll technology, I'm far more cautious now."
I breathed a sigh of relief, my tense body relaxing as I leaned back on the pillow.
"Great, then let's continue the experiment tomorrow! We need to finish it early! ♪"
"Oh, about that..." Persica propped her chin up with her free hand, "9, you don't have to stay in the lab anymore. It's no longer necessary."
No longer necessary?
"What do you mean?"
"Huh? What do you think I mean?"
"I mean, does it mean that I'm... I'm..."
Useless?

No.
Everyone is growing and changing.
I don't want to be the Doll that stays in one place, can't help, and is only taken care of by my family.

"9, what's wrong?"
"Huh? I..."
Persica's eyes focused on my hands, and I realized they were shaking.
"Is the new frame not compatible? It shouldn't be, there haven't been any issues so far..." Persica muttered as she turned on the instrument again.

"No, it's not a problem with my frame!"
Persica looked at me quietly, puzzled by my unexpected outburst; I didn't expect it either.
The thoughts generated by my neural cloud are too complex for me to process. I should... Right, I need to explain myself first—find an excuse quickly so that 45 and Persica won't notice...

"What's wrong?"
Persica and I turned to the door at the same time. High heels clicked on the metal floor as Miss Kalina walked in.
"9, are you feeling alright?"
"She's doing well enough, but she seems to have eaten something bad," 45 shrugged with a dispassionate smile.
"Eaten something bad?"
"I-I'm fine! Thanks, Miss Kalin," I quickly waved off 45's joke. "So, is there something you need?"
"Yes, I came to bring you something." Miss Kalina placed a box on my lap. I opened it to find some black fabric with orange accents inside; my favorite color combination.

"Are these... clothes?"
"Yes, they're custom-made for you. Wear this uniform to work tomorrow."
"Work? You mean—" I looked at her in confusion.
"Hasn't Persica told you yet?" Miss Kalina raised an eyebrow. "Starting tomorrow, you'll be the specialist in charge of communications, coordination, and daily affairs, 9."
Communications... specialist... me? I don't quite get it, but is Miss Kalin saying I can still stay here? Stay here... as I always have.

"Why me?"
"Considering everyone's personality in 404, you're the best fit for this post. Besides, we need someone... trustworthy for this job. Of course, despite the mundane-sounding job title, there will still be situations where you need to fight, so you won't get bored."
"What about the lab tasks?"
"I've collected most of the data here, so I don't need you to assist with the experiments all the time. If necessary, you won't mind if I occasionally borrow you during your 'spare time', will you?"
I see. So that's what she meant.

"Ah... yeah, sure." I relaxed and flopped down, stretching out on the bed.
"But remember to make an appointment in advance, I'm really busy. ♪"
Oh, speaking of Persica, she mentioned something just now... um... what was it...
"Oh, right! Persica, you just said I was attacked while I was talking to 45, didn't you?"
"Huh? Yeah, that's right..."
"I didn't have time to upload my neural data, which means... I don't remember what I talked about with 45!" I grabbed 45 urgently, "What did we talk about? Can you tell me again? Please~"
"Nothing, just some boring everyday stuff." 45 pushed my shoulders and sat me back down, then shoved the box of clothes into my hands. "Try on the new outfit."
She's clearly trying to change the subject! I puffed up my cheeks and held the new clothes up to myself.
"Not bad... Haha, your current image does make you more suited for missions in the sun, 9~ ♪"
Image?? Aren't 45 and I pretty much the same in that regard?
"What's so special about my image?"
"Nothing really." Persica looked at me blankly.
"Hmm...?"
Miss Kalina handed me a hand mirror. Puzzled, I took it and held it up to my face.

"My scar! My scar is gone!"
